Florida State Seminoles Louisville Cardinals NCAAF Louisville looks to get back on track following a second straight loss in ACC play when it hosts Florida State at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium tonight at 7 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Cardinals are 4.5-point home favorites, but my Florida State vs. Louisville predictions and college football picks for Friday, Oct. 9 expect the Seminoles' offense to take advantage of one of the country's worst defenses. Who will win Florida State vs Louisville: Florida State +4.5 Florida State is coming off a narrative-changing victory after beating Virginia by 31 points. The Seminoles have now covered in each of their last two games against FBS opponents, showcasing one of the country's best run games. With Ashton Daniels at QB and Ousmane Kromah at running back, FSU is 12th nationally in EPA per rush and 17th in rush success rate (49.7%). That could be a problem for a Louisville defense that's been one of the worst in the Power Four, allowing the 14th-most yards per game in the country (423). Daniels and Kromah have combined for 755 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns in five games, and if they get going on the ground, Florida State can turn this into a shootout on the road. I like FSU at +3.5 or better . TOP PICK Florida State vs Louisville Over/Under pick: Over 59.5 Louisville has an offense that looks capable of winning the ACC and a defense that looks capable of losing every game against a quality opponent. In four FBS games, Louisville has averaged 33.5 points per game and allowed 33.2 ppg. The Cardinals have hit the Over in three of those games, and I like them to do it again with a total of 60.5 or better . With Lincoln Kienholz expected to be healthy for Louisville, he should keep the offense humming. The Cardinals rank top 25 nationally in offensive success rate (49.7%) , and Kienholz has accounted for 15 touchdowns and a 77.2 QBR. Kienholz, along with running back Isaac Brown (and Keyjuan Brown if he plays), should push a Florida State defense that's 98th in rush success rate (46.9%) and 93rd in net adjusted EPA per play. Florida State vs Louisville combo Louisville's defense is the reason it's already lost three games this season and why it's failed to cover in two straight ACC matchups. Louisville doesn't create negative plays on defense, ranking third-last in the ACC in havoc rate (13.2%) and 88th in net EPA per play. With Kromah and Daniels carrying FSU's ground attack, they will be able to break loose for big plays and approach 30+ points. Meanwhile, FSU has defensive issues of its own, ranking 92nd in available yards percentage (52.1%) . A high-scoring game should lead to a back-and-forth final frame. Florida State +4.5 Florida State vs Louisville prop: Florida State team total Over 27.5 Florida State has scored 28+ points in four of five games this season, and Louisville has allowed 28+ points to all four of its FBS opponents this season. I'd play the Over on the Seminoles' team total at 27.5 or better . The Seminoles are averaging 33.2 ppg this season, and Kromah has quickly become one of the best running backs in the country. He ranks top 10 nationally in forced missed tackles on runs (28) and runs of 10+ yards (14). Daniels' mobility has opened up the offense, too, with the Auburn transfer sitting top 25 in the country in QBR (80.5) thanks to the damage he's doing on the ground. Pete Fiutak Wed, October 7, 2026 at 4:58 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's amazing how fast two weeks can change things. Louisville appeared to be ready to make a charge with a close loss to Ole Miss, a great 41-31 win over SMU, and winnable games coming up. A 30-27 loss to Wake Forest and a 31-28 loss to NC State later, and now the Cardinals have to win to stay alive in the ACC race. Florida State was done. Head coach Mike Norvell was all but fired, and then everything flipped. The Seminoles tuned up against Central Arkansas, and then stunned Virginia 38-7. Win this, and the season narrative totally changes. Florida State vs Louisville Quick Hits Florida State is on the road for four games in the next five, with a trip to Miami up next before hosting Clemson. Louisville goes to Syracuse next to start a run of three road games in four dates. Before the last meeting in the 2023 ACC Championship, the two teams split the previous ten games. How To Watch Florida State vs Louisville Date: Friday, October 9, 2026 Game Time: 7:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Louisville, KY – Week 6 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Expert Picks: Week 6 Why Florida State Will Win So what did Florida State do against Virginia to generate all of this excitement? The defense pitched one of its best games in a long time, considering the circumstances, holding the Cavalier passing game in check with a monstrous day from the pass rush. The Noles generated ten sacks and 12 tackles for loss. The relentless pressure should continue against a Louisville offensive front that's having a problem keeping teams out of the backfield. Why Louisville Will Win Can Florida State show up on the road? It's not quite fair to dog the Noles for losing at Alabama, but the program has lost 13 straight games outside of Tallahassee, going back to the win over Florida late in 2023. Louisville has to take a deep breath after the NC State loss. It played well. The ground game was great, quarterback Lincoln Kienholz was fine on his dinged up ankle, and everything was fine outside of three lost fumbles. Florida State hasn't forced a takeaway in a month. Florida State vs Louisville Prediction, Betting Lines Florida State isn't awful. The pieces are there – the ground game is solid, and look out if that pass rush keeps on rolling – but they have a hard time always fitting together. The Seminoles will crank up plenty of yards and points – the Louisville defense isn't anything special – but the offense will stall a few too many times, and the Cardinals will find their offensive scoring punch after two straight disappointments. Louisville 38, Florida State 30 Latest Consensus Line: Louisville -3.5, o/u: 59.5 ATS Confidence (out of 5) : 4 Must See Rating (out of 5) : 3.5 Consensus line based on BetMGM, Caesars, DraftKings, and FanDuel. Final prediction for Florida State vs. Louisville in a big Week 6 meeting
picks.blurb: Final prediction for Florida State vs. Louisville in a big Week 6 meeting Skip to main content Recruiting Women's sports Men's basketball Women's basketball Baseball & softball FanSided NCAA Sites Florida State is just a few hours away from kicking off Week 6 against the Louisville Cardinals in Kentucky. The Seminoles managed to improve to 3-2 last week in a major way, and the win allowed fans to enjoy Florida State football for a moment. Now, the next challenge awaits, and Louisville is a far different team compared to Virginia. Last week, Florida State entered the game as home underdogs against Virginia, and the team appeared to take that personally based on the response on the field. The Seminoles shifted the momentum of the game in the second quarter and never looked back afterwards. Securing a dominant win always feels good, but the reality is that Florida State still has plenty of work to do moving forward. Hosting the Seminoles this week will be the Cardinals, who are in the middle of a two-game losing streak against the likes of NC State and Wake Forest. Empty possessions have not been a problem for Louisville, but fumbles and the growing miscommunications on defense have. The talent is certainly there, but the results have not been, which makes Louisville a very dangerous team to play against. Can Florida State replicate the Week 5 success against Louisville? The expectations have now been set for Florida State after coach Mike Norvell proved this team can win dominantly. Now, the real test begins, and that involves repeating that performance against another strong ACC team in Louisville. It might be a rough start to the season for Louisville at 2-3, but the Cardinals' team is loaded with talent, particularly on the offensive side. Quarterback Lincoln Kienholz looked like a true Heisman Trophy candidate early and remains a very dangerous player despite the recent losses. Louisville is arguably the only team in the ACC that could potentially rival Miami offensively, and they will serve as a serious test for the Florida State defense. Virginia is a very experienced team, and Florida State found a way to shut them down on offense, but Louisville is not necessarily the same type of team. Kienholz and the Cardinals hurt opposing defenses through the air, which happens to be an area of weakness for Florida State. Expect a long night for both defenses during Week 6 Completely shutting down the Cardinals' offense is likely not going to happen, as the worst performance the offense had this season was good for 399 total yards and 27 points. The Louisville offense is a different animal, and that could pose a threat to the Florida State defense and the secondary in particular. With that in mind, Louisville could certainly have an explosive day on offense, but there is also a good chance that Florida State does the same. The Cardinals have the second-worst defense in the ACC, with an average of 29.2 points per game allowed. Louisville additionally allows 423 total yards per game, which means moving the football into scoring position should not be an issue for Florida State. Florida State has looked better defensively over the past two games, allowing an average of 226.5 total yards gained. The defense should be able to find enough success to prevent a blowout, but this game will likely come down to who makes the last mistake on offense. picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska is getting ready for a huge Big Ten matchup against Indiana, and Adam Carriker breaks down what the Huskers have to do if they want to pull off the upset and earn some serious respect. This is one of those games that can change the way people look at a team. Nebraska has put together a strong start, but now the Huskers get a chance to prove it against a ranked Indiana team led by Curt Cignetti. Indiana has been one of the best teams in the Big Ten, and this game will give Matt Rhule’s team a chance to show how far it has come. Carriker starts by looking back at the history between Nebraska and Indiana; he then shifts to Nebraska’s offense and quarterback Anthony Colandrea. If Nebraska is going to win this game, Colandrea will need to have a big day. He has to make smart decisions, take care of the football, and make plays with both his arm and his legs. Carriker also compares Colandrea to Indiana’s quarterback Josh Hoover and talks about why Nebraska needs to put pressure on Hoover and force him into mistakes. The Huskers’ pass catchers are another major part of the matchup. Nebraska has playmakers who can make a difference, and Carriker takes a closer look at players like Kwazi Gilmer and how they match up with Indiana’s defense. On the other side of the ball, Nebraska’s defense could be one of the biggest factors in the game. Rob Aurich and the Nebraska defense will need to be at their best, especially on third down. Indiana has talented receivers, solid running backs, and an offense that can hurt teams in several different ways. Nebraska cannot afford to give up easy conversions or big plays. One of the biggest topics in the episode is penalties. Nebraska had 16 penalties last week while Indiana had zero. That is a massive difference, and Carriker makes it clear that Nebraska cannot expect to beat a ranked team if it keeps hurting itself. Cleaning up the penalties is one of his biggest keys to the game. Carriker wraps up the show by laying out five keys for Nebraska: limit penalties, stop the run, play four full quarters, run the football, and limit big plays. None of those things are complicated, but Nebraska has to do all five if it wants to compete and win. The Huskers also need to be ready for a physical game. Carriker talks about trading blows with Indiana and matching the Hoosiers for all four quarters. This cannot be a game where Nebraska plays well for two or three quarters and then fades late. The second half will be huge. Carriker also throws in a little extra motivation with a beard bet if Nebraska wins. At the end of the show, he gives his final score prediction: Indiana 27, Nebraska 24. He sees it as a close game, but Nebraska will need a big performance from Colandrea, a strong game from the defense, and much cleaner football to pull off the upset. Learn inside info first, only on the Carriker Chronicles. Stay up to date on all things Huskers by bookmarking Nebraska Cornhuskers On SI , subscribing to HuskerMax on YouTube and visiting HuskerMax.com daily. Loading recommendations... Please wait while we load personalized content recommendations ADAM CARRIKER Adam’s dream of playing for the Huskers came to fruition. He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. Since retiring, he’s experienced great success in the business world and has also appeared multiple times on National Television and Radio Shows, and currently hosts his highly popular show, the Carriker Chronicles, aka, the People’s Show, which has been viewed by millions! With Ohio State on deck for the Hoosiers, will they take this matchup seriously? Let's dive into my Indiana vs. Nebraska prediction . My Week 6 college football picks expect the Cornhuskers to keep today's game competitive from start to finish as a 7.5-point underdog against the Hoosiers, who have yet to be tested by an explosive offense like this. For the full slate, see our Week 6 Top 25 predictions and best bets . It all kicks off Saturday, Oct. 10, at noon ET on FOX. TOP PICK Who will win Indiana vs Nebraska today? Pick: Nebraska +7.5 Are the Indiana Hoosiers playing underwhelming football to kick off the 2026 season, or are the books putting too much respect on them? Their record may show 5-0, but they're just 1-4 ATS, a sign this team could be underperforming in the early going. It's worth noting that all of those spreads have been between 20.5 and 57.5 points, a lot to ask even against teams the Hoosiers should beat handily. Are they simply coasting against their weaker opponents? They did seem to turn on the burners after a close call against Northwestern in Week 4, following that up by covering their first spread of the season with a 47-15 win over Rutgers as a 24.5-point favorite. Now, the Hoosiers have to travel from New Jersey to Lincoln to play the Nebraska Cornhuskers before heading back home to host No. 5 Ohio State in Week 7. Meanwhile, the Cornhuskers have been at home since returning from East Lansing on Sept. 26. This has look-ahead and tired legs written all over it. This game should mean a lot more to the Cornhuskers, who are looking to take down the reigning national champions, while the Hoosiers already have their eyes on the horizon. Give me Nebraska +7.5. Indiana vs Nebraska Over/Under pick: Over 48.5 With the travel, look-ahead spot, and this being a real test for both teams, points should come in bunches. Both teams are 3-2 to the Over this season, and both offenses can put up points in a hurry. The Hoosiers may have been limiting opponents to under 14 points per game, but the Cornhuskers are easily the best offense they've faced yet, one that's averaging just shy of 50 points per game this season . Now add in the travel and tired legs, and I expect this game to get ugly in a hurry. Indiana vs Nebraska combo Nebraska bringing it offensively correlates nicely with each of the three legs, and if you combo them all together to get your Saturday morning sweat going, you'd get a crispy 5.37x. Nebraska +7.5 Nebraska first half +4.5 Indiana vs Nebraska prop: Nebraska first half +4.5 The Cornhuskers have been able to score quickly through their first five games this season, averaging 25+ points in the first half. The Hoosiers, on the other hand, have played a much easier schedule and are averaging just under 20 points in the first half this season. However, Indiana is also allowing the fewest points in the first half, at just 11.5, as it should given its schedule. Factor in the look-ahead to Ohio State and the trip from New Jersey to Lincoln this past week, and the Hoosiers could come out a bit slow, giving the hometown team a chance to build some early momentum. Getting above a field-goal cushion in the first half, the Cornhuskers should be able to keep this one close and cover +4.5. picks.headline: Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Indiana
picks.blurb: Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Indiana - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Champions League results Fantasy Football Rankings for Week 6 NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit WNBA Finals games moved Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Indiana Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's midterms for Nebraska football following its best start since 2016. Now, the Huskers welcome Indiana to Lincoln for arguably the biggest game of the season for both teams. For Nebraska, it'll either finally get over the hump and snap its 30-game losing streak against ranked opponents or start another dreadful latter half of the season. For Indiana, it's either another win or its first loss since 2024. Though this is a matchup between two undefeated teams, the contrast is present. The Hoosiers are the defending national champions, while the Huskers still have yet to prove themselves. But other factors differentiate these teams, despite their many similarities. Though both teams have slow starts offensively, Indiana has been able to march downfield early in games, only to fall short in the red zone. For Nebraska, its early-game struggles come down to the offensive line needing time to find its footing. The Hoosiers can surely exploit that, considering they held Northwestern to 32 rushing yards on 27 carries. Now Indiana can swallow up the run again for Nebraska, whose top runner in the past two weeks has been Anthony Colandrea. The Hoosiers also got to Aiden Chiles four times, who is capable of taking off. Colandrea took two sacks against Maryland, so either he's going to be taking off or he's going to be tasting the turf a lot more against the Hoosiers. But if there is time in the pocket, Colandrea can make things happen. Indiana did allow Chiles to throw 22-of-29 for 293 yards, so Colandrea could put up similar numbers. But Colandrea isn't flawless in the air. Though he's thrown only one true interception, Colandrea has been off target at times. Josh Hoover's in a similar boat but has been clean through five games, with no interceptions. Now, with reports of winds being at 17 miles per hour come kickoff, both quarterbacks could be limited in the air. However, Hoover has been sacked six times in the last four games and has only 18 rushing yards. If the Blackshirts can pressure him, they can at least slow Indiana's passing game further. That only leaves Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr. for Nebraska. The duo combined for 1,107 rushing yards on 152 carries, averaging 7.3 per carry. That is a problem for the Huskers. They allowed a few big runs against Maryland and nearly 150 total yards. So, the Hoosiers can either deliver devastating blows or just chip away at the clock to get to Nebraska's defense. But that only looks at the team's execution on plays, and there are more factors to consider. The Huskers enter the game with 43 penalties after drawing 16 last week. Though there was some controversy regarding that game, 16 penalties in a game don't just happen. Nebraska has allowed teams to continue drives due to penalties or has ended its own drives due to penalties. Indiana has only gotten 17 on the season, so that's another area the Huskers can exploit. Overall, Nebraska has multiple ways to come out on top here. If the Huskers can get the run game going and shut down Indiana's, there's a chance. But the line's struggles and penalties take away some of their advantages. Plus, with that recent history and its current issues, Nebraska needs to truly take that next step if it wants to win. But that won't happen unless it comes out like a championship-caliber team, or the Hoosiers play their worst game of the season. But this game will feel like last year's Michigan game. Indiana won't blow out the Huskers like in 2024, but it will still get the win. picks.headline: 3 bold predictions for Indiana football at Nebraska
picks.blurb: 3 bold predictions for Indiana football at Nebraska - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Champions League results Fantasy Football Rankings for Week 6 NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit WNBA Finals games moved 3 bold predictions for Indiana football at Nebraska BLOOMINGTON, IN - SEPTEMBER 19: Indiana Hoosiers LB Rolijah Hardy (5) warms up prior to a college football game between the Western Kentucky Hilltopppers and Indiana Hoosiers on September 19, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images L.C. Norton Sat, October 10, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Indiana football is set for its second road matchup of the 2026 season, facing Nebraska on Saturday afternoon in Lincoln. Both teams enter the matchup undefeated at 5-0 and 2-0 in conference play. Ordinarily a record like that would likely result in an AP top-25 ranking for the Cornhuskers but basically nothing makes sense anymore and you've just kinda gotta roll with it. Here's three bold predictions for the matchup: Lee Beebe Jr. proves critical Indiana's new-look running game has left shredded defenses in its wake a both Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr. have looked excellent on the ground early on. Richard is absolutely the Hoosiers' lead back and deserves the honors that come with it, but Beebe Jr.'s role has proven critical, specifically against Northwestern. He looked great against Rutgers as well despite carrying an availability report injury designation into the game. He'll prove just as crucial against a Nebraska team that's had a tough go of defending the run at times. Richard looks like the Big Ten's best running back, but Beebe's carries being productive will make this one of the most fearsome backfields in the country. Anthony Colandrea tests Indiana's linebacker corps The last mobile quarterback Indiana faced was Northwestern's Aidan Chiles and that didn't go entirely well for the Hoosier defense. Indiana was able to limit Chiles and the Chip Kelly-led Northwestern offense more than most, for sure, but his escapability at the position was a tough task for Indiana's defensive line to generate the kind of pressure that leads to bad throws. More often, he was able to buy time with his legs to open up some passing opportunities downfield. Anthony Colandrea, Nebraska's quarterback, is also mobile and has punished defenses on the ground with his legs more than Chiles this year. This is the kind of situation where you're glad Indiana has seen a similar sort of player before and has film to correct what can be corrected. That said, while Indiana's defensive line is monstrous and its linebackers consistently make plays at the second level, I think Colandrea realllly tests the latter unit. Indiana's linebackers aren't necessarily built to contain mobile quarterbacks from a pure athletic standpoint, moreso to help run the defense and fly in from the second level. Are there ways of scheming around that? Yes. Does Indiana have perhaps the best schemer in the country running its defense? Also yes. Either way, this is something to watch for. Charlie Becker's biggest play isn't a catch Charlie Becker is known nationally for his incredible play out wide, hauling in just about any ball sent his way for huge gains time and again. More locally, he's also known for his ferocity in the run game. There just aren't a ton of receivers with Becker's size, strength and mindset as a run blocker. He treats it just as seriously as his role as a pass catcher, which was a huge asset to Indiana's offense last year and remains so this year. He'll be doing more downfield with a more explosive running game. Look for a highlight-reel style block from Becker here. Join the conversation! away.headline: Indiana's injury report spells trouble for Ohio State: AJ Harris, Daniel Ndukwe healthy for Hoosiers
away.blurb: In terms of starters, tight end Andrew Barker is the only long-term absence from Indiana's 1s. Barker has been absent since the Rutgers game and is without a timetable to return. Defensive end Daniel Ndukwe made his return to the field for Indiana during a comeback 20-17 win over Nebraska in Lincoln, which the Huskers were in control of for most of the 60 minutes. Ndukwe was out against the Scarlet Knights in Week 5 but made his return after just one game away. Ndukwe is one of the best backfield hunters on the roster. A.J. Harris also made his return against Nebraska after being out since Week 1. Curt Cignetti and Bryant Haines leaned on Jaylen Bell and Jamari Sharpe in Harris's absence. Harris took over in the second half after being eased into the action. The defense looked much improved late after Sharpe was targeted by Huskers quarterback Anthony Colandrea. The offensive line has several banged-up starters. Right tackle Phillip Daniels hasn't played since the Texas game. Right guard/tackle Austin Siereveld, perhaps the most NFL-ready member of the group, was out against Maryland. Ohio State isn't a healthy team heading into the Buckeyes' Big Ten game of the year against Indiana in Bloomington this coming Saturday. From the looks of it, the Hoosiers will be, though, outside of their long-term injuries. Other than that, the Hoosiers are getting mostly good injury news. A.J. Harris, Daniel Ndukwe make healthy returns against Nebraska All in all, Indiana's defense looked closer to whole during a trap game that nearly had the Hoosiers fully in the Big Red trap. Now, IU looks ready for a date with OSU, with a clean bill of health mostly, barring any issues in practice over the next week. Ohio State injuries could hold Buckeyes back in B1G title game rematch Ryan Day does not have the same luck with his roster. The Buckeyes are limping into Merchants Bank Field at Memorial Stadium. In their place, Jake Cook and Gabe VanSickle stepped up to start, though the returns weren't ideal, facing a less-than-threatening Terrapins defensive front, to boot. Meanwhile, there are multiple receivers (Brandon Inniss, Devin McCuin) and defenders (nickel Jay Timmons, linebacker Christian Alliegro) with uncertain statuses as well. away.blurb: Considering that Van Poppel looked like he wasn't adjusting all that well to Aurich's defense in fall camp and then surged into a situation where he was getting as many snaps as any defensive lineman in the last few weeks, it couldn't be a worse time for an injury to keep him out of Saturday morning's massive game. The good for Nebraska heading into the massive showdown against Indiana on Saturday is that the team is mostly healthy. Jamal Rule, Jacory Barney, and Mekhi Nelson are off the injury reports entirely. The bad news is that Thursday night's report added a defensive player the Huskers can scarcely afford to miss. Riley Van Poppel's apparent injury isn't a big deal simply because he's a defensive lineman, and the Hoosiers' run game is easily the best the Huskers have faced so far this year. His potential absence is also a big issue because Van Poppel's playing time has increased as the season has gone on. Van Poppel's use by Nebraska defensive coordinator Rob Aurich has, in fact, never been bigger than it has been since Nebraska started Big Ten play. Against Ohio, he saw just 30 snaps. WVU does have some things working in its favor with the Wildcats down key players at the skill positions in addition to playing abnormally early by their standards. ESPN's Bill Connelly's SP+ model doesn't think it will be enough, though, for the Mountaineers to get back in the win column, projecting a 34-24 victory for the visitors. I'm sorry...what??? West Virginia University Football | Christopher Hall - West Virginia on SI Look, I can fully understand Arizona being the projected winner, but only a combined 58 points? I'm not so sure about that. Yes, the Wildcats have been good against the run, but their blitz-happy nature makes them vulnerable to explosive plays in the passing game, which WVU has hit on consistently all year. And while they do have the 11th-ranked run defense in the country, they haven't quite seen a rushing attack like the one they will face on Saturday in Morgantown, which averages just a shade under 295 yards per game. The Mountaineers will move the ball and score points, just like Arizona will. If the final score ends up 34-24, I'd see it actually going WVU's way, believe it or not. This would likely mean that the Mountaineers are able to force a couple of turnovers, and the absence of Tre Spivey, Chris Hunter III, and Gio Richardson impacts Arizona's ability to be as potent through the air. Again, I don't see that being the case, just like I don't expect West Virginia to be held to just 24 points. What a loss would mean for the Mountaineers West Virginia University quarterback Mike Hawkins Jr. | Christopher Hall - West Virginia on SI Dropping to 3-3 is far from ideal, especially when you look at the remainder of the schedule - games against TCU and Texas Tech on the road, Houston comes to Morgantown, and then a road trip to Utah to end the year. Not to mention, going to TCU won't be easy. I'll keep saying it, though: With the way this offense moves the ball and puts it into the end zone, it makes the schedule not nearly as daunting as it may be with a shaky unit to go along with a struggling defense. There may be games that the Mountaineers win that they are not expected to because of that offense, and this weekend against the Wildcats could be one of them. Only eight teams in the country are better. Its 299.8 yards per game are the second most passing yards in the conference and 19 th in FBS. As for West Virginia, it’s ranked 15 th in the league and 121 st in the country in completion percentage. It is last in the conference in pass attempts at just 88. Its 178 ypg are also last in the Big 12. That ranks 117 th in FBS. The Mountaineers don’t defend the pass very well, either. They’re allowing 288.2 ypg, suggesting that Arizona could easily meet its average this week. That’s also last in the Big 12. Meanwhile, Arizona is giving up 75 ypg less at 213.2. WVU makes up for that by having the 3 rd ranked rushing offense in the country with 294 ypg on the ground, almost twice as many as Arizona’s 151.6 ypg. That’s a problem the Wildcats conquered just last week when Cincinnati came to town. The Bearcats came to Tucson averaging 270 ypg on the ground. Arizona held them to a season low of 74. None of the Bearcats’ runs went for more than 21 yards after breaking off 53-yard gains against both Miami (OH) and Kansas State the previous two weeks. The shortest “big run” they had prior to that was 31 yards in their season opener. The Wildcats also showed their defensive prowess on the ground against BYU, even if it didn’t result in the win. The Cougars average 235.5 rushing ypg, which is good for 16 th in the country. UA held them almost 90 yards under that at 248 in week two. BYU may lose some of its rushing luster over the next month with LJ Martin injured, but that doesn’t take away from Arizona’s effort against a full-strength Cougar running attack. Can Arizona reproduce that in a game that is across the country and likely has some extra emotional baggage for the WVU head coach? From a statistical standpoint, it’s definitely within the realm of possibility. While WVU doesn’t defend Arizona’s strength very well, the Wildcats do defend the Mountaineers’ strength well. UA has the third best rushing defense in the Big 12, allowing just 79 ypg. That comes in at 11 th in the country. Opponents average just 2.97 yards per rushing attempt. The negatives for Arizona are the travel, kickoff time, and the general emotion that’s likely to be on the other sideline. Stats say the Wildcats could win, but those things might make it closer than it would otherwise be. Ezra Amacher — Arizona wins 31- 28 Traveling to the Eastern Time Zone for a noon kickoff that’s really 9 a.m. for the visitors from Tucson makes this a trickier game to pick than it might appear on the surface. First, the opponent. West Virginia has been inconsistent at home under Rich Rod and its last game in Morgantown resulted in a 41-24 loss to Oklahoma State. The Mountaineers are in desperation mode after starting 0-2 in Big 12 play following last week’s crushing loss at Iowa State. Rich Rod indicated postgame that his defensive coordinator is having trouble fixing what’s broken. It’s safe to say West Virginia players and coaches are feeling the heat at the moment, and a third straight loss would a message for what direction the program is heading under Rodriguez. I think Arizona’s defensive game plan will go a long ways in determining the outcome of the game. If Danny Gonzales and his staff put forth a plan to stymie the Mountaineers rushing attack, then the Wildcats should leave with a hard-earned win. Considering how well last week went, I’m going to ride with Danny G and Co. until proven otherwise. Adam Green — Arizona wins 38 -24 Before the season started I had this game as a loss for Arizona. Much like my colleague Juan below, I felt like the Cats traveling across the country to face a RichRod offense — without even knowing the kickoff time — would be too much to handle. Then Arizona obliterated Cincinnati and West Virginia’s defense has shown to be, well, offensive. Understanding that Arizona may have some struggles without any of its starting receivers, I’m thinking the Cats should still have little trouble moving the ball and putting up points in this one. The only real question is if Danny Gonzales’ defense will be up to the task of slowing down an offense that, when it’s right, is incredibly difficult to stop. If Arizona can limit turnovers and create long fields for the Mountaineers there should be just enough opportunity to put some distance between the teams on the scoreboard, and given the early kickoff we should have a pretty good idea early on if this one is going to go the Wildcats’ way. Juan Serrano — West Virginia wins 35-27 I had this game marked down as a loss in my preseason record prediction. I was called crazy on social media for this prediction but now it is not looking so unrealistic that Arizona could lose on Saturday. This line of thinking is not due to the Wildcats not playing well or anything like that because through five games they have looked solid. It’s more so due to the fact that the Mountaineers are better than most people thought they would be. I saw West Virginia’s improvement coming and thought it could present an issue for Arizona. Fans in Tucson know just how much former head coach Rich Rodriguez loves to run the football, and this season he has his Mountaineers as the third best rushing attack in the country. Danny Gonzales ’ defense was up to the task last week against Cincinnati, but this is a whole new challenge. Michael Hawkins Jr. is a difference maker and can be dangerous both on the ground and through the air. I believe the secondary’s discipline will be tested in a major way this week, and will struggle. Noah Fifita will need to execute an efficient offensive performance to more than likely keep up with West Virginia on the scoreboard. If the run game can continue progressing as it has over the last two weeks, then Arizona could possibly control the clock. However, I believe that Rodriguez will have his guys motivated to play extremely hard after two very tough losses. The former coach of the Wildcats will get a little bit of payback on Saturday, and West Virginia will earn it’s first conference win of the year and move to 2-0 overall against Arizona. Brandon Combs — Arizona wins 38-21 I would be lying if I said that Morgantown was an easy place to play. Even so, there’s one glaring issue for West Virginia, their terrible defense. They haven’t faced an offense quite like Arizona and a QB like Noah Fifita . Last week, we saw what the Arizona offense can be when it is actually humming. And it looks great, even with three starting wide receivers out due to injury. If the offensive line has a good game, like I think they will, the running game will be able to establish some momentum and Noah will be able to pick the leaky Mountaineer secondary apart. Defensively, I think this game will be a challenge for Danny Gonzales. It would be silly to think otherwise. However, much like the offense, last week showed us what the defense can do when it’s operating on high octane. Gonzales’s crew played their most physical game and shut down a great Cincinnati rushing attack. I don’t think they’ll be able to shut down Rich Rodriguez’s run game, but I predict they will be able to disrupt it enough to degrade the offense. Michael Hawkins Jr. is a stud in the run game, but he isn’t much of an issue through the air. Arizona proved they can negatively impact a mobile quarterback last week, and I expect similar success this Saturday. Brian Pedersen — Arizona wins 38-34 Like Washington State, this is another game that I picked Arizona to lose prior to the season. But that was before I saw just how bad West Virginia’s defense is, and it’s bad. If the Wildcats don’t score more than 30 points in this game it’s because of their own mistakes, not for lack of opportunities. As good as the UA defense has been, and it’s been really good particularly against the run, to expect to shut down RichRod’s rushing attack is foolish. The man knows how to scheme a ground game, and if quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. can also complete some passes this will be a shootout. It will all come down to Noah Fifita and how he gels with the retooled receiving corps. away.blurb: West Virginia couldn't reach the end zone on several first-half scoring chances, including a short field goal, a lost fumble at the 2 and a turnover on downs at the 3. After the latter possession, Fifata was hit as he threw and was intercepted by West Virginia's David Afogho. West Virginia quarterback Mike Hawkins Jr. scored from 3 yards out on the next play. October 10, 2026 / 6:57 PM EDT / AP Noah Fifita threw two of his three touchdown passes to Isaiah Mizell, Lee Molette III returned a fumble for a score and Arizona beat West Virginia 52-31 on Saturday. Antwan Roberts, Quincy Craig and Kedrick Reescano each had scoring runs for the Wildcats (5-1, 2-1), who won their fourth straight despite missing their top three wide receivers, all of whom were injured a week ago in a win over Cincinnati. It didn't matter. Fifita and Mizell took advantage of a West Virginia secondary that has struggled all season, committed several interference penalties on Saturday and got burned in one-on-one coverage. "Holy smokes, Isaiah Mizell," Arizona coach Brent Brennan said. "I'm really proud of him. He was going to be ready for his opportunity." West Virginia defensive coordinator Zac Alley had decried his unit as "the worst defense in college football" after allowing an average of 593 yards in losses to Oklahoma State and Iowa State. Not much improved Saturday. "It's really frustrating," West Virginia coach Rich Rodriguez said. "We didn't get it fixed today, defensively especially. And then offensively, when we had a couple of turnovers, it really cost us, and we couldn't get the momentum we needed." Fifita completed 16 of 23 passes for a season-high 341 yards. Mizell, a sophomore, set career highs with six catches for 183 yards. He had entered the game with 176 yards all season. West Virginia (3-3, 0-3) has lost three straight. The Mountaineers wasted another solid effort from Big 12 leading rusher Cam Cook, who ran for 141 yards, including TDs of 1 and 30 yards. Cook couldn't handle an option pitch that went behind him and Molette scooped up the fumble and went 32 yards to put Arizona ahead 14-3. Mizell had a 14-yard TD catch in the first quarter. His 48-yard reception in the third quarter set up Reescano's 8-yard scoring run. And Mizell capped his big day by taking a short throw from Fifita over the middle and going 72 yards to boost Arizona's lead to 38-24 at the end of the third quarter. Fifita also had a 42-yard TD toss to Brandon Phelps on a trick play in the fourth quarter. Arizona is off to its best six-game start to a season since going 5-1 in 2014, when Rodriguez was their coach. He was fired following the 2018 season and returned to West Virginia a year ago for a second stint after going 60-26 with the Mountaineers from 2001-07. away.blurb: WVU Starting Corner Downgraded to "Doubtful" vs. Arizona - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF WVU Starting Corner Downgraded to "Doubtful" vs. Arizona A new availability report is out for West Virginia, and it's a mixed bag of good and bad news. With a potent offense like Arizona coming to Morgantown, you'd like to be at full strength defensively, but it looks like the Mountaineers will be down a starter, with arguably their top corner, Nick Taylor, downgraded from questionable to doubtful. The good news is that pass rusher Harper Holloman, who battled through a banged-up shoulder last week at Iowa State, is trending to be in uniform this Saturday. Arizona's offensive line has not been great in pass protection this season, giving up 15 sacks this year, which ranks 126th nationally - a great sight for a defense that has struggled to manufacture pressure since the start of league play. Having Holloman, the Mountaineers' best pass rusher available, is a big, big deal. When Noah Fifita is kept clean, he's completing nearly 80% of his passes for over 1,100 yards and 12 touchdowns. This is the one guy you can't allow to stand in the pocket and pick you apart. Who fills in for Taylor if he's downgraded to OUT? Keyshawn Robinson will likely still be a part of the rotation there, and maybe even Jaire Rawlison as well, who has seen limited action so far this season. The next availability report will need to be submitted by 10 p.m. ET tonight, and if Taylor is still considered doubtful, it at least gives a sliver of hope that he can go or at least be available. Mandatory Credit: Danny Wild-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Doug Joubert Thu, October 8, 2026 at 3:50 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Tulane 2026 Football Schedule 6:30PM, 10/16 In a battle of colors Saturday morning in West Point, the Tulane Green Wave open the defense of their American Conference 2025 championship by visiting the Army Black Knights. Both teams enter the contest at 2-2 on the season. Team Schedules The Wave has lost its road contests against ACC defending champion Duke to open the season, then versus Big-12 opponent Kansas State two weeks later. Sandwiched between and after the two trips were home contests against Sun Belt teams, which Tulane claimed victories in both: South Alabama in the home opener and Southern Miss two weeks ago. The Green Wave had an open date last Saturday before its conference opener this weekend. Army opened the season at home with a 56-point shellacking of Bryant University out of the Coastal Athletic. The Black Knights followed with an American Conference loss at Michie Stadium versus South Florida, an early open date, then a league victory at Temple before falling at Louisiana Tech last weekend. See the PFF comparisons between Army and Tulane here. The Black Knights opened a 3.5-point favorite over the Green Wave earlier this week. That number has dropped to 3-point Army advantage since Monday. As of this writing, 81% of the money bet is on Army, giving the points to Tulane. Tulane Has Something to Prove: Our On SI Tulane Prognostication This 2026 version of Green Wave football has, if anything, been consistently inconsistent. Open the season with your new starting quarterback, who is replaced after 30-minutes, whose replacement is replaced a little over two-and-half games later, and whose replacement of the replacement is replaced for one play. Show an erratic rushing offense that can slash opponents with gigantic games from various running backs, but have nothing on a regular basis . Big passing plays to big players, but with drops and throws that sometimes don't come close, showing communication and concentration issues. Offensive and defensive fronts that are growing and progressing, but is their growth rate fast enough? Stop an opponent with three-and-outs on defense on consecutive drives, then have huge rushing gaps open in the defensive front seven or wide open receivers in the secondary. To have this much variety in results is confusing and awkward. There is plenty of talent on this team. With 60-returnees from the 2025 playoff team and some solid additions, think Jaylin Lucas, Fat Hill, Macho Stephenson, Ed Smith IV , this team should be hitting stride. But it's not. Instead, it is showing how consistently inconsistent it can be, which you cannot do against a team like Army. The Black Knights are the least penalized team in the American Conference only getting 16-flags on the season. They are the 5th least in all the NCAA. They do not make mistakes. If you are inconsistent, the discipline of Army will expose that, and expose it quickly. No matter how much coaches and players talk about defending the Black Knights option, it's another thing to actually do it. To defend it will take that word we keep on bringing up: consistency. We have not seen that from this Tulane team this year. They have to prove that they can be a team that does things well and does them on a regular basis. They have yet to do so. We think the big play will be open for Tulane, as the Black Knights give up more yards per play than any other team in the American, almost 7-yards a pop. If the Wave offensive front is able to open the holes for the running back and protect the quarterback, whoever that may be (we believe it should be Trace Johnson , but we've been wrong before), there will be big chunks available. However, we also believe Army's multiple option attack will be the undoing of the Green Wave defense. On SI Tulane Pick: Army 35 - Tulane 28 Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. 2026 Week 6 Preview: Tulane Green Wave @ Army Black Knights
picks.blurb: 2026 Week 6 Preview: Tulane Green Wave @ Army Black Knights | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty October 13, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications American Conference Two high-powered rushing attacks meet in West Point for the first time since the 2024 American title game. Time and date: Saturday, October 10 at 12:00 p.m. ET Network: CBS Sports Network Location: Michie Stadium — West Point, NY Spread: Army (-3.5) Over/under: 48.5 All-time series: Tulane leads, 14-10-1 Last meeting: Tulane 24, Army 17 — October 18, 2025 Current streak: Tulane, 1 (2025) Setting the scene Even before sharing the American Conference, Army and Tulane were famliar opponents, squaring off 19 times from 1996 through 2020. The Black Knights then joined the American in 2024 and instantly ran the league, rattling off an 8-0 conference record before handling Tulane in the conference championship game. That was the only time in the last four years Tulane didn’t serve as the conference title host. With first-year head coach Will Hall in the fold, the Green Wave hope to host the American Championship for a fourth time in five years. To achieve that goal, it starts with defeating Army at Michie Stadium in this conference opener. Tulane Green Wave outlook Tulane (2-2, 0-0 American) split its non-conference slate, falling to Duke and Kansas State by double-digits on the road, while escaping Sun Belt opponents South Alabama and Southern Miss at home with late fourth quarter heroics. The biggest question entering this game, asks: who starts at quarterback? Zeon Chriss-Gremillion was Tulane’s Week 1 starter, but the Green Wave moved to Kadin Semonza for Weeks 2 through 4. But at the end of the last outing against Southern Miss, head coach Will Hall changed quarterbacks from Semonza to true freshman Trace Johnson in the fourth quarter. Johnson provided a spark in the come-from-behind victory, but his sample size remains small, completing just 2-of-5 passes for 35 yards without a single rushing attempt. The passing game unquestionably needs a boost. Tulane ranks 105th in the FBS in passing offense, completing just 54.2 percent of attempts with three touchdowns against one interception. The pass protection has been lacking too, allowing the 11th-most sacks per game in the country at 3.3. However, the Green Wave can dominate on the ground, and they do it with several different weapons. Running backs Jaylin Lucas and Maurice Turner each rushed for 200+ yards in the first four weeks, and the group gets even deeper as Jamauri McClure — Tulane’s starting running back during its 2025 College Football Playoff run — is slated to make his season debut. Tulane’s strength last season was its run defense, but the Green Wave have fallen off in that department, entering this matchup against the No. 1 rushing offense ranked 125th — allowing 191 yards per game on the ground. Losing star outside linebacker Chris Rodgers certainly doesn’t help, but the Green Wave still present veteran linebackers Makai Williams and Dickson Agu, who will be essential to countering this option. Army Black Knights outlook Army (2-2, 1-1 American) is already preparing for its third conference game. The Black Knights’ first two conference matchups were decided by the thinnest margins, featuring a lead change in the final two minutes. Army wound up on the wrong side of that late lead change in Week 2 when South Florida converted a late fourth down for a game-winning touchdown. But two weeks later, the Black Knights returned the favor at Temple. One-score games are customary for Army. Nine of the Black Knights’ last 10 matchups against FBS competition were decided by one score, and eight of the last nine were decided by four points or fewer — including every FBS matchup this season. Army’s option offense is in a familiar spot at first in the country in rushing yards per game at 334, while averaging the sixth-most yards per carry (6.4) in the FBS. Cale Hellums, who led all quarterbacks in rushing last year, remains the unit’s leading rusher with 301 yards, and his rushing performance dictates the result more than anyone else. In Army’s two wins, he has 191 yards and five touchdowns on a 6.6 average. In the losses to South Florida and Louisiana Tech, he combined for 110 yards and one touchdown on a 3.0 average. The Black Knights’ other ball carriers in the option attack include running back Godspower Nwawuihe and the explosive slot backs Samari Howard (293 rushing yards on a 10.9 average) and Zach Mundell (159 yards on a 14.5 average). However, Nwawuihe’s status remains unknown after he missed the Louisiana Tech game, which could make Carson Smith and Jake Rendina the downhill threats. Army’s defense allowed over 500 yards to Louisiana Tech, and that remains the team’s greatest struggle. The Black Knights are 89th nationally in yards allowed, while playing a style that typically limits possessions. Army has struggled with a lack of backfield pressure, producing the third-fewest sacks (3) and fewest tackles for loss (12) in the country. Additionally, the Black Knights are the only team yet to force a turnover. Army and Tulane are off to somewhat similar starts. Both are 2-2, highlighted by strong ground attacks and run defenses that need improvement. However, they sit on opposite sides of the time of possession spectrum, with Army ranking fourth nationally and Tulane third from the bottom. The Green Wave offense requires explosives in the run game, while the Black Knights move in a more methodical, sustainable fashion. Neither team is a proven passer, and Tulane may lean even more heavily on the run game than usual to keep its defense fresh. As usual, Army games come down to the wire. This will be no exception, and the Black Knights prevail at home in a low-scoring affair. If Texas can bring home the Golden Hat again, it would be the first time since the turn of the century that the Longhorns won three straight games over the Sooners. ESPN's College GameDay was in Tuscaloosa on Saturday morning to preview the Georgia-Alabama game, but it spent much of its time on the Red River Rivalry. But don't tell that conclusion to ESPN's Kirk Herbstreit, who thinks the ingredients are in place for a battle in this season's matchup. Herbstreit's Red River Pick While Texas is a solid road favorite against 2-2 Oklahoma, Herbstreit was thoughtful and reluctant to enter his decision on this game... before ultimately picking the Longhorns. Herbstreit certainly doesn't think the action goes down without a fight. "I think OU's going to make this game competitive," said Herbstreit on ESPN's College GameDay . "Because it's a rivalry game and you expect one team to win, that's always a dangerous receipe to me." Texas's Struggles QB Arch Manning could struggle, per Kirk Herbstreit, if Oklahoma can put him in long-yardage situations. (Randy Sartin-Imagn Images) | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Texas is the obvious favorite, but with two wins over ranked teams by a combined four points, the Longhorns haven't been a juggernaut, particularly on offense. QB Arch Manning has been underwhelming, currently sitting 10th of 16 qualifying SEC quarterbacks in QB rating. Manning's 7.5 yards per pass attempt ranks 11th of the passers. Manning is 14th in the league in passing yardage and his 7 touchdown passes ties for 11th. That said, Texas's offensive concerns still are minor compared to the issues at Oklahoma. Herbstreit Loves Oklahoma Defense Oklahoma is next to last in the SEC in scoring offense (22 points per game) and is dead last in total offense (321.3 yards per game). That's 57 yards per game behind 12th place Texas, and QB John Mateer has looked particularly lost with four interceptions on the young season and a performance so ugly against New Mexico that he admitted that he had to hear the crowd to clue him in on an open receiver on one play. While Oklahoma's offense has been woeful, Herbstreit notes, "Their defense has been playing at a championship level." Considering the occasional lapses in concentration from the Texas offense, Hebrstreit saw that as an advantage. "If they can get Arch [Manning] to 3rd and five, 3rd and seven, they can create havoc on him. They're one of the best third-down defenses in the country." Indeed, Oklahoma leads the SEC and currently ranks third nationally in allowing opponents to connect on just 23.1% of third downs (12 for 52). picks.blurb: Paul Finebaum Predicts Texas-Oklahoma Winner in Eye-Catching Fashion Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Paul Finebaum is many things, but not above a little casual trolling is certainly one of them. Known as one of the preeminent voices of SEC media well before his time began with ESPN, the network leans heavily on Finebaum's SEC expertise. And with the relatively recent expansion of the SEC, plenty of fan bases are getting to know Finebaum more and more. Add Oklahoma and Texas to that group, as the two former Big 12 stalwarts are getting to see more and more of Finebaum. This week on SEC Nation , Finebaum weighed in on the 2026 edition of the Red River Rivalry in his typical fashion. The four SEC Nation cast members weighed in on the Oklahoma/Texas game. Despite the show being in Norman, Oklahoma this week, the first three cast members went with the conventional wisdom and picked the Texas Longhorns who are favored by around a touchdown in the rivalry battle with the Sooners. Finebaum made it more interesting. Finebaum's Take "I keep hearing that you have a rivalry game and anything can happen. And you Sooners know that, right?" asked Finebaum. Having stoked the crowd, he then turned heel and disappointed them. "But I don't think you really have to factor that in because there's one team over here going up," continued Finebaum. "There's another team going down. And the Sooners are going down. Hook 'em, Horns!" THE PICKS ARE IN‼️ The SEC Nation crew make their picks for the Red River Rivalry 🤠 pic.twitter.com/8PCoNgnNNh Oklahoma's Troubles Finebaum delivered the unanimous vote for Texas and it's unsurprising as the top-ranked Longhorns travel to a 2-2 Oklahoma team that has had massive problems on offense this season. Since a 51-0 win over UTEP in Week 1, Oklahoma has scored just 10, 14, and 13 points in the past three games, which included a loss to Michigan and a 41-13 loss to Georgia. The Sooners failed to gain 300 yards in any of those three games. An 8-0 ESPN pick for Texas While Texas's offense has been somewhat inconsistent, the Longhorn defense has had enough strength to hold off Ohio State and Tennessee-- albeit by a combined four-point margin. While Oklahoma has an even more stout defense, the conventional wisdom is that a balanced Texas team can probably score enough points to win. While pregame pickers on both SEC Nation and College GameDay took time to shout out the OU defense , a unanimous 8-0 verdict between the two shows had the Longhorns winning. That said, few seemed to have as much fun in stoking the crowd as did Finebaum. Loading recommendations... Texas has beaten Oklahoma in three of Brent Venables' four Red River Rivalry games by an average of 32.3 points. In those three wins, the Longhorns held the Sooners to fewer than seven points, thanks to dominant defensive performances. This year's Texas defense might be the best one yet, ranking No. 3 in net adjusted EPA per play , No. 11 in success rate (36.5%), and No. 16 in havoc rate (20.6%). When the Sooners' offense doesn't score, the Under tends to hit at the Cotton Bowl, and this year's OU offense doesn't score (I like the Under down to 37.5 ). Oklahoma put up just 258 yards on Texas last year, and the Longhorns' defense is better this time around. It's ranked No. 5 by SP+ and has allowed more than 17 points once. That was to Ohio State and Heisman Trophy odds favorite Jeremiah Smith, and it allowed just three points in the second half to the Buckeyes. However, it's not just Oklahoma's offense that has struggled. Texas is averaging 22 ppg against Power Four opponents, and Oklahoma's defense is still feisty. The Longhorns' pass rush is one of the best in college football, with Colin Simmons ranking top 10 in the Power Four in pressures (18) and second nationally in sacks (7.5). Starting tackle Michael Fasusi is doubtful, while guard Eddy Pierre-Louis is questionable. If Oklahoma can't establish the run, Texas can force the Sooners into predictable passing situations, which will lead to fewer carries for Avant. Prop pick #3: Elijah Thomas Under 16.5 receiving yards According to Pro Football Focus , Sooners sophomore wideout Elijah Thomas ranks 964th among 996 qualified receivers , and I'd play this Under d own to 15.5 . Thomas was a four-star recruit coming out of high school, but he has mostly earned offensive opportunities because of his special-teams prowess. away.headline: Oklahoma Sooners' injury report for matchup vs. Texas Longhorns opened eyes to an issue that's been going on since 2024
away.blurb: The Oklahoma Sooners head into the Red River Rivalry against the Texas Longhorns with a long injury list. At this point, what's new? Banged-up rosters have become the norm for OU over the last few years. Ever since the SEC's player availability reports started in 2024, the Sooners have almost always carried a health disadvantage into game day. George Stoia of SoonersScoop.com pointed out a number that puts it in perspective, and I think it's worth mentioning. Stoia laid it out: OU averages 10.25 players on the initial availability report since it began in 2024. Its opponents averaged 6.68. OU has had fewer players on the initial report only once-the College Football Playoff game against Alabama. The Sooners had 6 players on that report. That feels about right. Nobody needs to stat-check it, either. Thursday's availability report for OU vs. Texas tells the same story . The Sooners have five players listed as out, two doubtful, one questionable, and five probable. Oklahoma – Out: Taylor Heim, Trell Harris, Xavier Robinson, Jacobe Johnson, Fred Hinton – Doubtful: Trynae Washington, Michael Fasusi – Questionable: Eddie Pierre-Louis – Probable: Jer'Michael Carter, Cole Sullivan, Michael Boganowski, Owen Heinecke, Jack Van Dorselaer. Texas – Out: Kaliq Lockett, Jordan Coleman, Zion Williams – Questionable: Justus Terry That's 13 names for Oklahoma and four for Texas. That's just how it is for the Sooners every week. When the Wednesday report came out, some fans were legitimately concerned. The list looked worse than it did heading into the Georgia game, even though OU had a bye week in between. More names showed up after a week off, not fewer. So fans scrambled to figure out how a team gets more injured during a bye. Fair enough, that's a decent question to ask. How does that work? I have no idea. Most likely, some players got more banged up in the Georgia game, and we just didn't know about it going into the bye. That's why building depth in the NIL era matters so much. You're going to have injuries, and OU seems to have more than anybody. Maybe that perception is right, maybe it's wrong. Regardless, the depth has to be better. You can sit here and look at this issue all you want and try to figure out what's going wrong internally. The game still has to be played. Texas isn't going to skip the Red River Rivalry because Oklahoma has a lot of guys on the report. You'd love to see the Sooners keep building their depth so the next man up can carry more of the load. For now, the Longhorns definitely have the advantage. Texas is already the No. 1-ranked team in the country, and the Sooners are coming in with really bad football. With 13 players on the availability report, OU will need its backups to step up. home.headline: Michael Fasusi injury update: OU football OL 'just about ready' to return to Sooners
home.blurb: Sooners coach Brent Venables said Tuesday that left tackle Michael Fasusi is "just about ready" to return. Venables added Fasusi has to clear another hurdle or two in the next few days but that he should be ready to be back "soon." Fasusi was initially listed as doubtful to play against Texas last week before being ruled out. The second-year linemen played in 11 games and made 10 starts last season as a true freshman, allowing four sacks on 395 pass-blocking snaps, per Pro Football Focus. "Nobody wishes they're playing more right now than Michael Fasusi," offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle said. "You should see him at practice. He's always encouraging with great, great energy, great juice. Even whenever we're at a little bit of a low man, he's out there just yelling, 'Thank you, Jesus.' I'm like, OK, I got it. You're right. Thank you, Jesus." "He's great with scheming out things, how they play, how they do what they do," Arbuckle said. "It says a lot about a coach and he does a fantastic job." This article originally appeared on Oklahoman: Michael Fasusi injury update: OU football OL 'just about ready' to return to Sooners NORMAN — Oklahoma could be getting perhaps its best offensive player back soon. "I'm excited," Venables said. "Everybody's excited to get another really good player back and he's worked relentlessly. He's in great shape. You saw him in pregame, amped up and ready to go." He appeared to reinjure his shoulder in the Sooners' season-opening win over UTEP after he dealt with an injury during training camp. Getting Fasusi back would do wonders for OU's offense against No. 15 Kentucky at 6:30 p.m. Saturday at Gaylord Family — Oklahoma Memorial Stadium . Venables said he doesn't compare the Sooners' lists with other teams but OU doesn't tackle to the ground in practice and tapers its practices back as the season goes along. McElroy took the Ducks 31-21 on his Always College Football podcast and built the pick around a red-zone trend for Oregon coach Dan Lanning. Still, Lanning hasn't cleared the former UCLA quarterback, and the Big Ten's first injury report for the game is due Wednesday night. Raiola replaced Moore at the Coliseum and went 19 of 25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns. However, McElroy pointed to the Nebraska transfer's history against ranked teams. "If you look back at his time at Nebraska, he was 0-5 against ranked football teams," McElroy said. "Well, UCLA is ranked." A Raiola start would also come one week before Oregon faces Nebraska. Running back Wayne Knight, who followed Chesney from James Madison , has 445 yards and nine touchdowns on 49 carries against FBS opponents. McElroy noted the Bruins average 7 yards per carry, the best mark in the country. But Oregon has allowed just nine runs of 10 or more yards. The Bruins' passing game is the concern. Quarterback Nico Iamaleava has thrown four touchdown passes, which McElroy said ranks 118th nationally, and Chesney's teams struggle when they have to lean on the pass. "Bob Chesney is 20-1 as an FBS head coach when his team runs fewer than 30 pass plays," McElroy said. "He is 1-3 when they have to throw it 40 or more times." Why did McElroy pick Oregon? The Bruins come in after a dominant start to the season, a fast-rising program under first-year head coach Bob Chesney. The Ducks will rely on backup quarterback Dylan Raiola to build on his strong performance in a win over USC two weeks ago. Here is a preview of Oregon vs. UCLA: No. 13 Oregon (3-1, 1-0 Big Ten) vs. No. 21 UCLA (4-0, 2-0 Big Ten) When: Saturday, Oct. 10 Time: 12:30 p.m. PT Where: Autzen Stadium Latest line: Oregon by 11.5 Radio: Oregon Sports Network Stream : You can watch this game live with Fubo (free trial), or with DIRECTV (free trial). Oregon's first, second and third priority defensively is to stop UCLA's potent run game. The Bruins rank No. 4 in the nation in rushing offense at 281.5 yards per game, led by dynamic running back Wayne Knight with 49 carries for 445 yards and nine touchdowns. Quarterback Nico Iamaleava's ability to extend plays with his legs can't be ignored, either, and the Ducks will likely be without safety Aaron Flowers, who is listed as doubtful as of Thursday night's availability report. Oregon's vaunted defensive line needs to plug the gaps on the interior, and its edge rushers and linebackers need to prevent big plays to the outside. UCLA can run it any direction, any time with Knight and backup running backs Anthony Woods and Jaivian Thomas. Raiola dazzled in a 41-27 win over the Trojans, stepping in for the injured Moore to go 19 of 25 for 289 yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions. He's had two weeks working with the ones during Oregon's bye week and the lead up to this week's game, and the Ducks are confident in his ability to captain the ship. The UCLA defense thrives in bringing simulated pressures, which could throw Raiola off if he's not ready to change plays at the line or adjust on the fly. But he has shown a deep understanding of Drew Mehringer's system in his two appearances so far this season, and arguably his best throw of the day against USC — a bomb to Dakorien Moore for a touchdown — came under pressure. Raiola is a gunslinger, and this Bruins team will provide the biggest test yet of his apparent growth in not putting the ball in jeopardy. OPTIONS GALORE There is no shortage of weapons for Raiola to work with on Saturday, even with the injury to wideout Jeremiah McClellan. Top tight end Jamari Johnson had two weeks to get even healthier after a stellar game against USC, and the Ducks get freshman receiver Jalen Lott back this week after a broken hand during fall camp. Plus, regular starters Evan Stewart, Messiah Hampton and Dakorien Moore are all feeling confident after connecting with Raiola on several big plays against the Trojans. This offense should have little to no drop off without Moore on the field, as long as the Ducks make necessary in-game adjustments against a well-coached Bruins defense. And they will likely need to run the ball effectively as well. This year's meeting comes at an interesting time for both programs. UCLA has been one of college football's darlings this season. After being picked to finish 13th in the Big Ten, the Bruins are off to a 4-0 start, punctuated by a 54-3 trashing of Maryland. Meanwhile, Oregon was the No. 2 team in the preseason AP Top 25 and Coaches Polls and a favorite of many to win the national championship. However, it had a closer-than-expected victory over Boise State and then lost to Oklahoma State as a heavy favorite. Since then, it has responded with a win at USC. Additionally, the loss in Stillwater has aged well as Oklahoma State has played itself into the Top 20, so the Ducks remain a viable threat to make the playoffs. Now, with UCLA's emergence, they have a chance to pick up another quality win. Oregon has won 14 of the last 17 meetings, including 34-13 in the lone meeting as Big Ten programs two years ago. This time around, Oregon is a double- digit favorite at home. With a total approaching 60 points, there could be plenty of points on the scoreboard. UCLA vs. Oregon Odds Last season, Oregon finished 11th in the FBS at 36.9 points per game, and it's up to fourth this season at 47.5 points per game. Even if you throw out the 84-point outburst against Portland State, the Ducks have still scored at least 31 points in every game this season. One reason is that Jordan Davison usually marches into the end zone. After his third win over USC , Dan Lanning used his post-game press conference to recruit, telling players in the fertile recruiting ground of Los Angeles to come to Oregon instead of play for the Trojans. Should the Ducks win this weekend, he will likely have a similar message, but Davison is one of the Ducks who has already made the trek to Eugene. The Santa Ana native has scored 23 touchdowns in 18 career games. He has found the end zone in 14 of his 18 games, including each of the first four games. Many of them are short, as the 236-pounder is Oregon's preferred option on the goal line. However, he has been proficient at getting in, as he is averaging one touchdown every 8.1 carries. Oregon's team total this week is 35.5 points. One path to getting there is scoring five touchdowns, and if so, Davison likely scores at least once. Maurice Jones-Drew is one of the greatest Bruins of all time and went on to have a great NFL career despite standing 5-foot-6 inches tall. The Bruins may only have Wayne Knight in Westwood for one season, but some around the program are comparing him to MJD. While that is lofty, Knight enters this week averaging 111.2 rushing yards per game on 9.1 yards per carry. Like Davison, Knight has scored in every game this season. He is tied for third in the FBS with nine rushing touchdowns. With UCLA being a double-digit underdog this week, there is a bit more value on Knight this week than you would expect for someone with nine touchdowns in four games. While I like Oregon to win at home, it hasn't been as dominant defensively as expected. Against the three FBS opponents it has faced, Oregon has allowed 27 points in all three games. It ranks 46th in Rushing Success Rate Allowed and 64th in Rushing Explosiveness Allowed. Obviously, Knight has been a big-play threat, averaging nine yards per carry. He has recorded at least one 30-yard carry in all four games this season. Knight could score on an explosive touch or use one to set up a short touchdown in the red zone. Either way, I like him to find the end zone for the 10th time this season. UCLA enters this week 91st in passing yards allowed, giving up 225.8 passing yards per game. It is stepping up in class this week as it takes on a prolific Oregon offense. Oregon is getting 225 yards per game from its receivers alone. Dakorien Moore has been a key contributor for the Ducks with 14 receptions for 234 yards and four touchdowns. The sophomore has recorded 40 receiving yards in each of his first four games, clearing 50 in two of them. With Jeremiah McClellan sidelined for the foreseeable future, there may be even more volume to go around. McClellan is not the only notable injury for the Ducks this week, as star quarterback Dante Moore remains out with a concussion. However, Oregon is one of the few teams in the country that can truly say it has two starting quarterbacks given Dylan Raiola 's experience at Nebraska . Raiola came to Oregon to sit behind Moore for a year, but he was ready when his number was called, going 19-for-25 for 289 passing yards and two touchdowns. As good as Dante Moore is, Oregon should see very little dropoff with Raiola under center, and he is well-equipped to exploit this UCLA secondary. The Bruins are 17th in Passing Success Rate Allowed, but 133rd in Passing Explosiveness Allowed. Dakorien Moore is averaging 16.7 yards per catch, so he may only need a few catches to clear this line. Additionally, Raiola's passing yards line is 291.5 this week. If he approaches 300 yards again, I like to get Moore to record at least 50 of that total. One reason many fell in love with "PAC-12 After Dark" is the wild, high-scoring games that cap the slate. UCLA and Oregon were no exception, as the last 10 meetings have averaged 64.9 points. The over is 6-3-1 in that span. UCLA has quickly become a profitable team to back for overs, 3-1 to the over this season, and all three overs have gone 69 or more. First-year head coach Bob Chesney has remade the Bruins offense, which has scored 45 points in three of its first four games. However, it also allowed 38 points to Purdue , whose offense is far less prolific than Oregon's. As mentioned, Oregon's team total is 35.5, and I like the Ducks to clear it and potentially reach 40 points. A similar spot for the Ducks came when UCLA's crosstown rival came to Eugene last season. Oregon was a 10.5 point-favorite over USC with a total of 59.5 points and it won 42-27, covering and comfortably clearing the over. The Ducks are 4-0 to the over this season and 8-2 over their last 10 games dating back to last season. One of those games was a 53-34 victory in the CFP over James Madison, when Chesney was the head coach. Now with UCLA, I think Chesney will get his Bruins to score enough to help Oregon clear the over.

In a devastating setback for UCLA’s Nico Iamaleava and his team, the quarterback is expected to miss a significant amount of time after getting sandwiched by two defenders Saturday. A prolonged absence of UCLA’s starting quarterback could imperil the unbeaten Bruins’ bid for their first appearance in the College Football Playoff. In his first appearance with UCLA after transferring from Cal Poly, Dieffenbach completed three of six passes for 43 yards while effectively managing the offense. Chesney said after the game that he had gone with Dieffenbach instead of Madden Iamaleava – who had previously appeared in relief of his brother this season – because of the superior ability to run the ball that Dieffenbach had displayed in practice. The last time that LSU played in Lexington, it didn't go very well for the Tigers. LSU lost 41-21 on the road to Kentucky in 2021. It was the second straight SEC loss for the Tigers under then head coach Ed Orgeron. It was a loss that all but sealed the fate of Orgeron (especially after he admitted that LSU's defensive line got out-physicaled). The Tigers will return to Lexington this weekend for a matchup against the Wildcats. And while no players remain on the roster from the 2021 LSU team, I'm sure head coach Lane Kiffin will use the loss to Kentucky in 2021 as motivation. "I like this game being at Kroger Field," said Cubelic . "I like the momentum Kentucky has right now. The problem is that Kentucky can't get to the quarterback, and I think Sam Leavitt has gotten better in the pocket — he was forced to (get better in the pocket) with the hamstring two weeks ago against Texas A&M. And he did it again last week. "[Leavitt] being able to find success from the pocket and Kentucky not being able to get home, that's going to be a problem. And LSU is going to score. So I think LSU gets the win. I'm not going to touch the 8.5 (points) there that LSU is favored by, but I may like the over 51.5 in this game."
