The Trust Project What is this? LAS VEGAS — After five games of relative good health for North Dakota State, the Bison received pay back against UNLV on Saturday at Allegiant Stadium. The Bison lost leading rusher DJ Scott to a possible shoulder injury in a 13-7 loss to UNLV , something head coach Tim Polasek could cost the running back "a week or two." "He really had a hard time opening up and running but there was no structural damage as far as the lower back," Polasek said. In addition, starting cornerback DJ Voltz was on the sidelines in the second half with his elbow taped and his pads off. Scott left the game in the first half and appearing to favor his right shoulder. Scott went to the tunnel with someone from the NDSU medical staff. "There was a significant AC joint," Polasek said. Scott, a junior who's in his second year at NDSU after transferring from Kennesaw State, led the Bison with 298 yards on 70 carries and 4 rushing touchdowns. Sophomore Myles Mitchell took over the top running duties for the Bison. Mitchell played his first game since leaving the victory at Sacramento State with an injured ankle late in the third quarter. Senior Brady Wavrunek filled in for NDSU's final series of the first half and had 3 carries for 21 yards. The officials had a busy day, especially in the first half. NDSU was flagged seven times for 59 yards in the first 30 minutes while UNLV drew 4 penalties for 40 yards. The Bison's first half put them on pace to top their season-worst 13 penalties for 94 in the season opener against Jacksonville State at the Fargodome. picks.headline: Bold Predictions for Georgia-Alabama Showdown
picks.blurb: Bold Predictions for Georgia-Alabama Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Alabama Crimson Tide and the Georgia Bulldogs will face off on Saturday and are going to have to weather both the storm of each other and Hurricane Isaias. As always, this matchup brings memorable moments. It brings drama. It brings instant-classics. I have to find a way to get bold with it. I lost out on all three of my bold predictions for the Vanderbilt game after hitting on one against Oklahoma. Fortunately, I have seen this movie plenty of times. Here are three bold takes for the game between Kirby Smart’s Dawgs and Kalen DeBoer’s Crimson Tide that I think can legitimately happen. 5 Total Turnovers Between Both Teams The ground will be wet, the wind will be hard and the rain will be coming down. The weather is projected to calm down for actual gametime, but now tabbed as Hurricane Isaias is going to make its mark all the way up the state of Alabama. You know what that means: sloppy football. We already saw the Georgia Bulldogs struggle with fumbles during the rainy Western Kentucky game in the second week. I suspect that could be an issue again if the weather truly is complicated. Alabama’s quarterback Keelon Russell, as good as he is, has not faced a defensive unit as talented or as violent as Georgia’s. He has been pretty clean this year, throwing only two interceptions and losing only one fumble to this point, but I predict he turns the ball over at least once himself. I would probably predict that even without the weather. Turnovers happen when these two teams face off. The weather will induce more of them. I am predicting five will come true. Gunner Stockton Scores Two Touchdowns on the Ground Georgia’s redshirt senior quarterback has yet to score a touchdown with his legs this season – something he did 10 times in 2025, leading the Dawgs in that category. I think he will do it twice on Saturday night. Stockton has not carried the ball near as much this season as he did at this point a year ago. He exploded for almost 100 yards on the ground at Arkansas thanks to a career-long 62-yard run. Georgia also hasn’t played in a big game yet. Stockton’s legs were a favorite in their important matchups a season ago. The danger comes in the red zone for opposing defenses. He had a red zone rushing touchdown against Tennessee. He ran two in against Kentucky. He scored the dagger with his legs against both Texas and Auburn. He ran one in from 22 yards out against Ole Miss in the regular season and then ran for two scores against the Rebels in the Sugar Bowl. I think Stockton will find the end zone again, and I think it will happen twice. It is the piece of Georgia’s red zone offense - which is extremely multiple - that hasn’t been dished out yet this season. Nate Frazier has his first 100-Yard Game of the Season Especially because of the potentially awful weather, I think Georgia is going to run the football a ton. Nate Frazier has gotten his rest since getting dinged up against Arkansas. He was off to a super hot start that has been slowed down due to him virtually missing 2.5 games. Chauncey Bowens has been ruled out for this game due to a foot injury he suffered last weekend. Even with the emergence and explosiveness of Dwight Phillips Jr., Frazier will likely see the bulk of the touches out of the backfield. Georgia operates a committee-style running back room, and Smart keeps saying that Georgia will continue to spread the football around. Frazier is still the lead back, and he will have his touches increased in big games. Loading recommendations... picks.blurb: Bryce Young, Nick Saban, ESPN's College GameDay Make Picks For Alabama-Georgia Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THINGS BAMA FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM ALABAMA BASKETBALL NEWS ESPN's College GameDay chose Tuscaloosa to host this week's pregame show as No. 6 Alabama is facing No. 2 Georgia at Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday at 6:30 p.m. CT on ABC . The analysts on College GameDay closed the three-hour morning show from Coleman Coliseum by picking the winner of this top-10 SEC showdown. Former Alabama head coach Nick Saban is one of the analysts, alongside Desmond Howard, Pat McAfee, Kirk Herbstreit and host Rece Davis. They are also joined by a celebrity guest each week, with Saturday's being former Alabama and current Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young . So, which panelists picked Alabama over Georgia, and how many chose the Bulldogs over the Crimson Tide? Note: Davis, the host, doesn't make picks, and the same is said for Herbstreit, who is on the call tonight. Desmond Howard: Alabama Nick Saban: Alabama Bryce Young: Alabama Pat McAfee: Georgia Saban : "You know, I think Georgia's got one of the most complete teams in the country. I love Kirby, he's had a very consistent identity with his teams — tough, physical and all of that. But I really like the togetherness of Alabama's team this year, so I'm going Roll Tide, baby." Young : "Seeing how well a team plays together here at Bama, watching the togetherness, the secondary gelling with all of the turnovers they're creating, and I think the X-factor is Keelon Russell. Watching him develop, watching how well he's playing, watching him have command, I'm a huge fan, I think he's super special. So, of course, Roll Tide." Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer joined the College GameDay set for a segment earlier in the show and was asked if there's something that the college football world doesn't see that makes him believe in the Crimson Tide. UA started the season ranked No. 13 in the AP Top 25, but is now 5-0 and the No. 6 team in the renowned poll. "There’s a third field that we don’t practice as much on, but it’s where the grind happened in the offseason. And I think just the lessons learned and the things that we went through, the guys have this belief and trust because they know that everyone’s doing the work." Alabama's Practice Field 3 was a staple of the summer, and BamaCentral spoke with nine different Crimson Tide players about the haunting workouts that occurred there. Alabama leads the all-time series against Georgia 45-27-4, with the first matchup occurring on Nov. 2, 1895. The Crimson Tide has a 24-13-4 home record against the Bulldogs and has won eight of the past 10 overall meetings. However, Georgia has had the last laugh, beating the Crimson Tide 28-7 in the 2025 SEC Championship Game. Alabama finished with -3 rushing yards and was without multiple key players. It was just the second time that season, with the other being the previous Oklahoma matchup, that the Alabama defense did not force a turnover. It was the second time Alabama faced the Bulldogs in 2025, as the Crimson Tide won the first game 24-21 in Athens. Loading recommendations... Please wait while we load personalized content recommendations HUNTER DE SIVER Hunter De Siver is the lead basketball writer for BamaCentral and has covered Crimson Tide football since 2024. He previously distributed stories about the NFL and NBA for On SI and was a staff writer for Missouri Tigers On SI and Cowbell Corner. picks.blurb: Paul Finebaum Makes Georgia vs. Alabama Pick, Names Kirby Smart's Major Problem Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN analyst Paul Finebaum says Saturday’s top-10 showdown carries more weight for No. 2 Georgia than No. 6 Alabama, pointing to Kirby Smart’s winless regular-season record against the Crimson Tide. “It’s bigger for Georgia because Georgia has an Alabama problem, and so does Kirby Smart,” Finebaum said Friday on ESPN’s “Get Up.” Alabama has won every regular-season meeting since Georgia’s overtime win in Tuscaloosa in 2007. Kirby Smart’s Alabama regular-season drought Georgia Bulldogs head coach Kirby Smart lifts the SEC Championship trophy after the game against the Alabama Crimson Tide during the 2025 SEC Championship Game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Finebaum dismissed Georgia’s 28-7 win over Alabama in last season’s SEC Championship Game. Finebaum dismissed Georgia’s 28-7 win over Alabama in last season’s SEC Championship Game. “I’m well aware, Greeny, that Georgia won the last game. It was in the SEC Championship Game, and all my Bama friends say, ‘We were banged up. We weren’t ready to play.’ Well, big deal,” Finebaum said. “But the problem is that Kirby Smart has yet to beat Alabama in the regular season.” Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer has won both of his regular-season meetings with Smart, 41-34 at Bryant-Denny Stadium in 2024 and 24-21 in Athens last season. Finebaum also raised the streak on Wednesday’s “Get Up,” calling a third straight loss to DeBoer “ almost unthinkable when you think about Kirby Smart as being the premier coach.” Will weather affect Georgia vs. Alabama? Alabama and the SEC monitored Hurricane Isaias all week as forecasts called for heavy rain in Tuscaloosa. Finebaum doesn’t expect the storm to factor into the 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff on ABC. “The storm is long gone,” Finebaum said. “I’ve read weather maps more this week than I have read books on how to grow more hair, Greeny, and it’s just not going to be a big deal. The grass at Tuscaloosa drains about as well as Augusta National.” Finebaum picks Alabama over Georgia Alabama Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell (12) passes the ball during the third quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Finebaum took Alabama, as did ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky, while Joe Fortenbaugh and Harry Douglas picked Georgia. Finebaum took Alabama, as did ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky, while Joe Fortenbaugh and Harry Douglas picked Georgia. “I think this Alabama team is so complete,” Finebaum said. “Georgia has a slightly better defense, but the fact that we’re talking about Alabama in the same category is important. Alabama’s offense has been explosive.” Alabama ranks first nationally in offensive success rate, and Finebaum gave the quarterback edge to Keelon Russell , who has 11 touchdown passes and two interceptions. Georgia’s Gunner Stockton has thrown 13 touchdowns and one interception. “Take nothing away from Gunner Stockton. He’s really played well, but he’s not the best quarterback in this game,” Finebaum said. “Keelon Russell can manage a game like I’ve never seen from a freshman, and they have a good running game.” Georgia will also play without running back Chauncey Bowens, who was ruled out after getting hurt against Vanderbilt. Bowens has 164 rushing yards and six touchdowns on 35 carries. “Georgia has lost one of its top two running backs,” Finebaum said. “That’s a big deal in a game like this.” “Georgia has an Alabama problem, and so does Kirby Smart.” 👀 @finebaum on why this is a bigger game for Georgia 🏈 pic.twitter.com/omVAoIrWki Loading recommendations... Best Georgia vs Alabama props Prop pick #1: Keelon Russell Under 238.5 passing yards Despite my belief that Georgia will come out on top in this matchup, Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell will likely struggle through the air in Week 6, even if he's forced to play from behind. Prop pick #2: Gunner Stockton Over 199.5 passing yards Georgia hasn't leaned heavily on its passing game early this season, with just 44.53% of its plays coming through the air. Georgia is fresh off a smackdown on Vanderbilt, 38-14, while Alabama dismantled Mississippi State 56-23. This has game of the year potential, and there's been a lot of them in the SEC already! Georgia has the No. 1 rated offense and defense per PFF, averages the most points in the country, and allow the third-fewest rushing yards per game (57.4) — and all of that will be put to the test against Alabama. The Bulldogs pitched a second-half shutout against Vanderbilt and won 38-14 after leading 21-14 at the half. Georgia has allowed 20 or fewer points in all five games and 44 points over the last three games against Arkansas, Oklahoma, and Vanderbilt. The offense put up 471 total yards of offense, doubled Vanderbilt's first downs (26-13), and held the Commodores to 85 rushing yards. Alabama is coming off arguably their most impressive performance of the season. The Tide destroyed Mississippi State, 56-23, never trailing in the game. Alabama outgained Mississippi State in yards 483-302, went 6-of-9 on third downs, and forced four turnovers (2 INT, 2 Fumbles). Keelon Russell had another dominant outing with 301 total yards and four touchdowns (3 pass, 1 rush). Russell is climbing the Heisman Trophy rankings and a win over Georgia would likely jolt him to the top spot. Alabama has owned the series against Georgia winning 10 of the past 12, but the Bulldogs won the previous matchup 28-7. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch Georgia vs Alabama Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Time: 7:30 PM Eastern Site: Bryant-Denny Stadium City: Tuscaloosa, AL TV/Streaming: ABC Game Odds for Georgia vs Alabama The latest odds as of Tuesday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: Georgia Bulldogs (+102), Alabama Crimson Tide (-122) Spread: Alabama -1.5 (-112) Total: 52.5 points #2 Georgia Bulldogs Head Coach: Kirby Smart 2026 Record: 5-0 (3-0) Offensive Points Per Game: 51.4 PPG (1st) Defensive Points Per Game: 13.4 (12th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 97th 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 20th The Georgia Bulldogs Offense: Georgia is the highest scoring offense in the country which is odd because in years past, Kirby Smart has taken is foot off the gas against early season opponents. Georgia's scored 45, 41, and 38 points against SEC opponents so far with 471, 464, and 306 total yards of offense. Georgia ranks sixth in third-down offense (54.9%), fifth in passing efficiency (188.72), and 13th in turnover margin per game (+1.2). One area that will be of interest is Georgia's red zone offense is 51st in the country with a 25-of-28 conversion rate (89.3%), but the fourth-most red zone attempts. Georgia has to be aggressive in the red zone at Alabama. Field goals likely won't cut it. Georgia Player to Watch on Offense: QB Gunner Stockton In last year's SEC Championship Game, Gunner Stockton threw for three touchdowns on 20-of-26 for 156 yards. Georgia cruised 28-7. This matchup won't be as easy and could feature double the points. Stockton tossed three touchdowns versus Vanderbilt last week after combing for two touchdowns in the two weeks prior. Stockton hasn't been asked to do much this season due to all the talent around him, including the running back committee. Stockton has a 13:1 TD to INT ratio this season and a 75.7 completion percentage. The Georgia Bulldogs Defense: Georgia's allowing 244.6 yards per game (7th) and that will likely go up after this showdown. We know Georgia is great at getting pressure (PFF rank of 22 for pressure) or getting coverage sacks (PFF rank of 3 for coverage), but the two areas that will determine the game is third downs and red zone defense. Georgia's defense has a 33.8% third-down defense (44th) and have only allowed 11 red zone trips this season, but 10 of them have resulted in points (8 TDs, 2 FGs). Georgia Player to Watch on Defense: LB Chris Cole Chris Cole is a projected first round pick in the upcoming draft as a three-year player for Georgia. Cole opened the season with a half-sack, and added anther against Oklahoma with two fumble recoveries. Cole had 60 tackles last season, ranking fourth, and a team-leading 4.5 sacks. Cole has 22 tackles and 1.5 sacks to this season. Last year, Cole had five tackles versus Alabama and a sack. away.blurb: Alabama football suffered multiple injuries on Saturday against Georgia. The Crimson Tide most notably saw wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams take a hit to the head and never return to the 20-17 loss to the Bulldogs . home.blurb: “With Racin, just with his injury, lower-leg injury, we’ll just continue to evaluate him and see where he’s at in the days ahead. So obviously he’ll be pretty sore and kind of working through things and limited, for sure, early in the week... When Delgatty went out, Mal Waldrep began playing center for the Crimson Tide. He competed for a starting guard job this offseason, but lost out to Will Sanders. If Coleman-Williams is out, Alabama has some depth at receiver that could move up and contribute. Rico Scott is an obvious option, along with Cederian Morgan and Derek Meadows, and Grubb said Noah Rogers is close to 100% after his offseason injury. Alabama football coach Kalen DeBoer gave an update on injuries to three Crimson Tide players during his Monday press conference. DeBoer spoke on Ryan Coleman-Williams, Racin Delgatty and Terrance Green, ahead of the Tide’s Saturday trip to Tennessee . “Ryan’s got a couple things going on, work through an injury with his knee that’s been kind of going on, and we’ll deal with that,” DeBoer said. “Got the head issue as well. Gonna address that... this week, and pretty good chance we wouldn’t have him this weekend, I think it’d probably be week-to week after that. “Terrance, just keep evaluating his injury. Has been going on for a couple weeks now.” Delgatty went down late in the fourth quarter of Saturday’s game. He took over as the Crimson Tide’s starting center this season, after transferring in from Cal Poly. If Delgatty can’t go and Waldrep becomes the starting center, it would be bad for offensive line depth as a whole. He has been a key contributor at guard, with Sanders battling injuries at times this year. On Monday, Ryan Grubb said that Waldrep is the next man up at center. He struck a hopeful tone about Delgatty’s availability. “We’ll see what happens with Race,” Grubb said. “They braced it up at the end, but we’ll see. Jeff (Allen) is working his tail off to see what we can get.” Coleman-Williams went down with what appeared to be a left leg issue late in the first half of Saturday’s game. He has been wearing a knee brace on his right leg. After halftime, the junior wideout returned to the game. He left for good with a head injury after taking a helmet-to-helmet blow that was not called as targeting. Green, who has made an impact on the defensive line, was injured against Mississippi State, DeBoer told reporters after the game. He left the Georgia matchup after reaggravating the issue. He's been around the team some, and he knows what his priorities are right now, and that's trying to get healthy." (Photo: Benjamin Wolk, 247Sports) The big question on the injury front for Georgia this week concerns wide receiver Isiah Canion , who has been working his way back from a leg injury. What time? 8:10, so I'm sure y'all are sitting on the edge of your seat waiting to get it. You're dying to get it so you can write another article about it. "You guys are awesome about following those things up. I wait for y'all to write about it so I can find out about the other team. I don't even check it myself. So it'll be out Wednesday at 8:10, maybe a little later." (Photo: Icon Sportswire, Getty) Georgia will be without Thomas Blackshear for the foreseeable future. The sophomore suffered an apparent injury to his right shoulder during Saturday's game against Vanderbilt. He re-appeared on the sideline in the second half with his arm in a sling and was ruled out on the Wednesday availability report this week. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 19 USC desperately needs a win to remain in the CFP hunt, while Penn State looks to avoid a 0-3 start in the Big Ten Imagn Images It's a must-win game for both teams , as No. 19 USC travels to take on Penn State on Saturday in Happy Valley. Penn State enters the game with its season seemingly spiraling out of control. After a 3-0 start in nonconference play under new coach Matt Campbell, the Nittany Lions have dropped their first two Big Ten games, and didn't look particularly inspiring in either. The offense struggled mightily in losses to Wisconsin and Northwestern , and last week, the defense was gashed by Northwestern's rushing attack. Suddenly, a schedule that was considered one of the easiest in the Big Ten before the season began looks far more difficult for the Nittany Lions. Not that things have been much easier for their opponents. The Trojans are 5-1 on the season and are coming off a win, but have looked shaky for three straight games. They found themselves in a shootout with Rutgers three weeks ago, followed that up with a 14-point home loss to Oregon , and last week flirted with disaster against a Washington team that hadn't looked impressive to start the season. Now they're on the road against a team with its back against the wall, and a second loss (with Ohio State and Indiana still to come) could crush USC's playoff chances. USC vs. Penn State: Need to know It's the White-Out game: Penn State's White-Out game is a newer tradition in college football , having begun in 2007, but it's quickly become one of the games Penn State fans look forward to most. Everybody in Beaver Stadium is dressed in white and screaming at their absolute loudest. Unfortunately, the results haven't always matched the intensity. Penn State is only 11-7 in White-Out games, but that's partly because the Nittany Lions reserve the tradition for their toughest games. It's a battle of the two winningest QBs in college football: That fact probably caught you by surprise, didn't it? Well, it's true. Penn State's Rocco Becht comes into this game with 29 wins as a starting QB in his college career. That's more than any other QB in the country. USC's Jayden Maiava is tied for second with 24. So Becht will either widen the gap this week, or Maiava will narrow it. Penn State hoping to avoid a 0-3 start in Big Ten again: Last season, the Nittany Lions started 0-6 in Big Ten play. It was an unexpected slide that led to James Franklin's mid-season firing. If they lose here, they'll be 0-3 in the Big Ten for the second straight season. The last time that happened was the 2003 and 2004 seasons. Of course, Matt Campbell could take some solace if his team loses. He'd be the first Penn State full-time head coach to start his tenure with a 3-3 mark since Joe Paterno in 1966. I don't like either side of the total, so I'm being asked to back a Penn State team that's looked terrible lately as a favorite, or take a USC team that's really struggled on the road under Lincoln Riley as a small dog. Frankly, there's no right option here, and I don't recommend taking any side. But, unlike you, I don't have a choice, so I guess I'm less terrified of USC +1.5 than anything else. But will enter one of the nation's loudest venues: Beaver Stadium in State College, Pennsylvania, the home of the Penn State Nittany Lions. USC Looks Ready to Embrace the Noise USC already cranked up the volume during practices for the Penn State game, literally. Students walking around the campus heard lots of crowd noise coming from the Trojans practice field. That's because USC blared that energy through the loud speakers. Even true freshman edge rusher Luke Wafle admitted to being spooked by the sound. "It scared me the first time they were doing sound checks, and I was walking out of my class," Wafle told reporters on Oct. 8. Wafle sounds locked in on preparing for the noise levels, though, along with the rest of his Trojans teammates. This marked the first time USC practiced with noise this season. While Riley isn't familiar with how loud Beaver Stadium is, he knows the Lions' coach well. That's because Riley and Penn State coach Matt Campbell faced each other before, in the Big 12 Conference. The Saturday, Oct. 10 matchup marks the seventh time the former Oklahoma coach, Riley, will face the ex-Iowa State leader, Campbell. But it'll be the first time they meet in the Big Ten. Riley owns the upper hand in the head-to-head matchups against Campbell's Cyclone teams, going 4-2 all-time against him and ISU. But Riley already knows what to expect from a Campbell-led team . "Going back to Iowa State, they've always used their tight ends really well, and they're doing so here [Penn State]. Defensively, they look a lot like the past Penn State teams in being big up front," Riley said during his Oct. 5 appearance on Trojans Live. "They've got really good athletes and talented players, and they're excellent on the back end. It's a well-coached football team, and it'll be a heck of a night." Meanwhile, PSU has delivered mixed results in "White Out" contests, going 11-7 overall there. However, most college football fans likely remember what happened the last time PSU fans wore white for a nationally ranked foe. Oregon blocked out the noise and won in double overtime to prevent a Penn State home win. And the Ducks turned to a silent count on offense to withstand the noise. Perhaps USC rolls with something similar in this showdown. But Riley's past success against Campbell, plus USC showing signs of resurgence on defense, should be enough to avoid the upset. picks.headline: College GameDay makes picks for USC vs. Penn State whiteout
picks.blurb: The No. 19 USC Trojans enter Saturday night’s clash against the Penn State Nittany Lions at Beaver Stadium with their College Football Playoff hopes on the line. The Trojans will play in one of their most hostile environments this season: the Nittany Lions' annual whiteout game at Beaver Stadium, which is in primetime on NBC , with kickoff scheduled for 4:30 p.m. PT. The Trojans are currently the underdogs, despite the Nittany Lions suffering two straight losses to the Wisconsin Badgers and the Northwestern Wildcats. DraftKings Sportsbook lists the Trojans as 1.5-point underdogs against the Nittany Lions. That didn’t stop a majority of ESPN’s College GameDay crew from picking the Trojans to beat the Nittany Lions as a road underdog. Here’s a look at the GameDay crew’s picks. ESPN College GameDay Predictions Desmond Howard: USC Nick Saban: USC Pat McAfee: Penn State Bryce Young (guest picker): USC Kirk Herbstreit: USC Can USC Pull Off a Statement Road Win Over Penn State? Despite being underdogs and struggling on the road under coach Lincoln Riley, USC’s offense has been among the Big Ten's best this season. Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava, who is in his second season as USC’s full-time starter, enters Saturday night’s matchup against the Nittany Lions as the Big Ten’s leading passer with 1,744 yards, 15 touchdowns, and three interceptions. Two of those three interceptions came in the Trojans' last two games against the No. 13 Oregon Ducks and Washington Huskies, which could be a concern for USC’s offense against the Nittany Lions, as one turnover could be costly in a game like Saturday night’s with Penn State. The Trojans are also depleted at wide receiver, which has always been a strength of their offense under Riley. The latest season-ending injuries to Corey Simms and Terrell Anderson are crushing blows to the Trojans' offense that will affect them in Saturday night’s game against USC. A pair of freshmen, wide receiver Trent Mosley and tight end Mark Bowman, are also listed as questionable for the primetime matchup against the Nittany Lions. Their potential absence will be yet another crushing blow for the Trojans' offense. Facing such a hostile environment on Saturday night against the Nittany Lions, it’s crucial the Trojans start fast and avoid mistakes early on in the game. In their 25-21 home win over the Washington Huskies at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Week 5, the Trojans offense got off to a slow start and even trailed by 11 early in the third quarter, before scoring 15 unanswered points to win. This is something the Trojans can’t afford to let happen on Saturday night when they face the Nittany Lions at Beaver Stadium. USC looks for its first win over Penn State as a member of the Big Ten, as the two last met in 2024 in Los Angeles, a game the Nittany Lions won 33-30 in overtime. A tough loss to Oregon was okay, but the wheels came off with six straight defeats, leading to an overhaul of the program. There's no need to fully panic quite yet, but after collapsing against Wisconsin in a 24-20 loss, and being run over by Northwestern by 21, this is a must-win moment with a trip to Michigan up next. USC got over its loss to Oregon with a great win over Washington, but there's a problem. If a road date at Penn State is your easiest game in the next month … USC vs Penn State: Quick Hits USC is starting a run of three road games in four, getting a week off before going to Wisconsin. Then it hosts Ohio State and then goes to Indiana . Penn State alternates road and home games until mid-November, going to Michigan next before getting a week off to get ready for Purdue. Penn State won 33-30 in the last meeting in 2024. USC won the two meetings before that in the 2009 and 2017 Rose Bowls. How To Watch USC vs Penn State Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: NBC Location: Beaver Stadium, University Park, PA – Week 6 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Expert Picks: Week 6 Why USC Will Win USC has a running game, and it has to get it moving in this against a Penn State defensive front that was ripped to shreds by Northwestern. Temple was able to run for over five yards per carry in its 27-9 loss to Penn State, and Wisconsin managed to average just over four yards per pop in its win. And then Northwestern and offensive coordinator Chip Kelly found something that worked, running the ball 55 times for 413 yards and four touchdowns. USC will try to win with the short passing game – Northwestern's Aidan Chiles completed 71% of his passes last week – but if it commits to the run with well over 30 carries, it'll work. Why Penn State Will Win USC doesn't generate enough pressure from its defensive front, and that gives mobile quarterbacks plenty of chances to hit the midrange passes on the move. Penn State's Rocco Becht might not be devastating when he runs, but the offense is deadly when he's connecting. Defensively, chalk up the Northwestern game to a bad day. The Nittany Lion defense is great on third downs, and it's third in the nation in pass defense. However … USC vs Penn State Prediction, Betting Lines Penn State hasn't seen a passing game like USC's. The Trojan defense is shaky, and it has to prove it can hold up on the road after having issues against Rutgers a few weeks ago, but Jayden Maiava and the Trojan passing attack will be strong throughout. But USC won't run well enough. Embarrassed by the Northwestern game, Penn State comes out roaring and holds up through a fun four-quarter fight. picks.blurb: Final score predictions for Penn State's Week 6 game vs. USC - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Champions League results Fantasy Football Rankings for Week 6 NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit WNBA Finals games moved Final score predictions for Penn State's Week 6 game vs. USC Kevin McGuire, Paul White and Christopher Sheppard, Nittany Lions Wire Fri, October 9, 2026 at 12:03 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Enthusiasm for the Penn State whiteout game may have fizzled out in recent weeks after Penn State jumped out to an 0-2 record in Big Ten play after last week's debacle against Northwestern, but a primetime game in the national spotlight could be the perfect time for Penn State to reignite the season. Penn State hosts USC on Saturday night as the Trojans make their first visit to Beaver Stadium since 1994 and for the first time as a Big Ten opponent. The Trojans bring a dangerous offense to the game but are faced with some concerns about the defense. Can Penn State find its offense against the Trojans and pull off a big win against a ranked opponent in the whiteout game? Here are our final score and player of the game predictions for Penn State's Week 6 game against USC, along with some brief thoughts on the matchup. Kevin McGuire, Lead Writer The last couple of weeks have set off some serious alarms for me about Penn State, and that does not fill me with a great amount of confidence in the Nittany Lions going into this matchup against USC. The Trojans have struggled with the defense this season but I'm not seeing the firepower necessary to keep things too competitive with the Trojans on Saturdya night. After Northwestern ran all over Penn State's defense, I think the Trojans would be smart to try mimicking that with King Miller setting the tone on the ground and allowing Jayden Maiava to do his thing with the passing game. Kayden Dixon-Wyatt of USC will be a problem all nigth for the Penn State defense. Final score prediction: USC 27, Penn State 20 Player of the game pick: Jayden Maiava, USC quarterback Paul White, Contributor This hurts to predict, but I just don't see a way Penn State wins this game. The offense should be able to get back on track against a weaker defense, but if we couldn't stop Northwestern's offense, then I'm terrified to see what USC does. Final score prediction: USC 38, Penn State 27 Player of the game pick: Chase Sowell, Penn State wide receiver Christopher Sheppard, Contributor It feels like the gig is up for the Nittany Lions. What should be a celebration of one of college football's greatest modern traditions could turn into a State College massacre. I don't think that there will be much resistance from the blue and white, but I could see young edge talent Yvan Kemajou flashing some potential. Final score prediction: USC 37, Penn State 20 Player of the game pick: Yvan Kemajou, Penn State defensive end Follow Nittany Lions Wire on X and Facebook . (Photo by Randy Litzinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jared Slanina Thu, October 8, 2026 at 11:07 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Nittany Lions seek their first win in Big Ten play after stumbling to an 0-2 start. in conference play. Penn State (3-2, 0-2) vs. USC (5-1, 2-1) Kickoff: 7:30 p.m., Beaver Stadium, State College, PA The Betting Line: Penn State -1.5 (Fanduel) TV: NBC, 7:30 p.m., Noah Eagle (play-by-play), Todd Blackledge (analyst), Kathryn Tappen (sideline) Weather: A cloudy day with a high of 67, with temps dropping into the upper 50s during the evening. Matt Campbell: PENN STATE RECORD: 3-2, 1st Year OVERALL RECORD: 110-72, 15th Year Lincoln Riley: USC RECORD: 40-19, 5th Year OVERALL RECORD: 95-29, 9th Year VS. PENN STATE: 0-1 Tony Rojas is the only active player with more than 21 career TFLs and six career interceptions…Saturday will be the 19th full stadium white out in Beaver Stadium history…USC and Penn State are both in the top 10 in program wins and winning percentage…USC leads the all-time series 6-5 over Penn State…the two programs will be meeting for the second time as members of the Big Ten. Jayden Maiava is one of the best quarterbacks in the nation when he heats up. The likely future first round draft pick has continually improved in three years as a starter, and is enjoying his best season up to this point. He is completing 69% of his passes with 15 touchdowns and three interceptions, and is on pace to set career highs in just about every category. Maiava has accomplished this without wide receiver Trent Mosely, who was quickly establishing himself as one of the nation's best receivers as a true freshman. He has been out with an injury since week two, and is not likely to return on Saturday. The Trojans still have their typical number of playmakers at the skill positions. Kayden Dixon-Wyatt, a freshman with the body of a veteran NFL receiver, has become the primary targets with 25 catches for 372 yards and three scores. Zacharyus Williams, another big-bodied receiver, has been a dangerous deep threat and is coming off his best game. Maiva also looks to tight end Mark Bowman often, a freshman who has become more involved with the offense in recent weeks – although he is questionable with an undisclosed injury. King Miller returns to the USC offense after rushing for just under 1,000 yards as a true freshman. He came back bigger and faster, and can be hard to take down at 6-0, 225 lbs. He can also be dangerous in the open field despite his size, and has a run of at least 20 yards in each of the past four games. Waymond Jones is another big, physical back who excels in short yardage situations. Penn State's defense appeared to be the strength of the team, and one of the best in the Big Ten. However, that sentiment was erased by Northwestern on Friday in of the poorest defensive performances in recent memory. The Wildcats put up 406 rushing yards, averaging 7.5 yards with each carry. Northwestern was able to run so freely that they only had 14 passing attempts while controlling the clock. It doesn't help that they will be facing a coach in Lincoln Riley that excels at creating offensive gameplans, and was just handed a blueprint for how to move the ball on the defense. It's hard to find any current point of optimism for the Penn State offense. The tackles have been unable to set the edge. The interior line is unable to open up running lanes or keep the pocket clean. The running backs have failed to find explosive plays, or provide a consistent ground game. Tight end Andrew Rapplyea and center Brock Riker are both playing through injuries that are obviously limiting their play. The receivers have shown promise, but don't get many chances because of all the off-target passes and balls regularly getting knocked down at the line of scrimmage. Rocco Becht has not yet shown he is capable of moving the ball against a Big Ten defense through two games. Despite being the nation's most experienced quarterback, he has often looked lost within the offense once the level of competition improved. Fortunately for Penn State, they are facing a defense that has been struggling after a positive start in non-conference play. The Trojans are ranked 14th or worse in the Big Ten in scoring defense, pass defense, total defense, and explosive plays allowed. USC gave up 30 points against Louisiana, 35 against Rutgers and 41 to Oregon in consecutive weeks. They are coming off a better result against a Washington offense decimated by injuries, holding them to 21 points and a key stop in the final minute to preserve the victory over the Huskies. If Penn State can find some rhythm, it may be against this defense. Safety Christian Pike is USC's most productive player, and should be on an NFL roster next season. He leads the team with 35 tackles, and has an interception and two pass breakups. Similar to Penn State, USC has a pass rush by committee and do not seem to have a dominate pass rusher who regularly makes plays in the backfield. Penn State fans will also recognize a couple of former Nittany Lions who transferred to USC over the off-season in linebacker Ta'Mere Robinson and defensive end Zuriah Fisher. SPECIAL TEAMS USC kicker Caden Chittenden is 6-of-7 on the season, with a career-long of 52 yards in 2024 while playing at UNLV. Punter Lachlan Carrigan is as consistent as they come, and has an average of 49.3 yards per punt. Penn State kicker Ryan Barker missed his second field goal of the season on Friday after not missing a single field goal that was not blocked in 2025. Barker has a career high of 49 yards, which he has hit on multiple occasions. Punter Nathan Tiyce is averaging 41.6 yards per punt this season, and is coming off a shaky performance against Northwestern with several short kicks. USC-27, Penn State-17 Maybe Penn State is able to prove they are better than the team we've watched in the last two weeks. Maybe there are some quick fixes to set things right. But for now, it appears the Nittany Lions are lost and searching for answers that may never come. It could be this team just isn't good enough to beat a quality opponent. Penn State will likely come out fighting and be boosted by the White Out crowd. However, my prediction comes to one simple fact – USC's offense can move the ball. Penn State still hasn't proven they can do so.

away.headline: Penn State week 6 injury report vs. USC: Who’s in, who’s out, and who has to step up
away.blurb: Penn State football takes on No. 19 USC in the White Out Saturday night. This Week 6 contest heading into the season was considered a pivotal game for the Nittany Lions (3-2, 0-2 Big Ten) as it was expected for them to be in a good spot after Week 5. While that ended up not being the case, they still have an opportunity to upset the Trojans and pull off a statement White Out win at home. Ahead of the matchup, both teams released their injury reports. Not much is different for the blue and white, but USC has a few questionable players that could give Penn State an advantage on Saturday. Tatsch is the most notable injury update on this list. He was listed as questionable earlier in the week, but was downgraded for Saturday's contest officially to "Out." While Tony Rojas and Kooper Ebel anchor that linebacker room, Tatsch's absence is more notable in comparison to someone like Smith who was also downgraded in last week's injury report vs. Northwestern. That room still has Cael Brezina, but it will be Rojas and Ebel picking up a majority of the workload without Tatsch or Smith. Nnodim and Tatsch were the "Questionable" players earlier in the week, and now it's just Nnodim. The defensive tackle has played in three games for Penn State since Week 3 vs. Buffalo. He's logged eight total tackles and one tackle for loss. If Nnodim isn't good to go or is limited on Saturday in terms of snaps, defensive coordinator D'Anton Lynn might put a little more on Keanu Williams and Siale Taupaki. The two lead the Nittany Lions' tackle room in total tackles so far this season and have the most NCAA experience. Ty Blanding, Alijah Carnell, and Dallas Vakalahi haven't been impact players for Lynn, so it'll be interesting to see which one will pick up the pace against the Trojans to help out Williams and Taupaki. Notable USC injuries: Jahkeem Stewart, Trent Mosley, Mark Bowman, and Jide Abasiri listed as QUESTIONABLE The junior starter on defense has had 16 tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss, and one sack on the season (six games). If Abasiri is limited or downgraded to out before the game, Stewart's likelihood to step in and be an impact on the defense when also listed as questionable is doubtful. Another notable injury is starting left guard Hayden Treter listed as doubtful for Saturday night. He played in the first five games for USC as well as Kaylon Miller. Miller stepped in Week 5 vs. Washington as Treter was questionable and ultimately did not play. home.headline: Penn State week 6 injury report vs. USC: Who’s in, who’s out, and who has to step up
home.blurb: Penn State football takes on No. 19 USC in the White Out Saturday night. This Week 6 contest heading into the season was considered a pivotal game for the Nittany Lions (3-2, 0-2 Big Ten) as it was expected for them to be in a good spot after Week 5. While that ended up not being the case, they still have an opportunity to upset the Trojans and pull off a statement White Out win at home. Ahead of the matchup, both teams released their injury reports. Not much is different for the blue and white, but USC has a few questionable players that could give Penn State an advantage on Saturday. Tatsch is the most notable injury update on this list. He was listed as questionable earlier in the week, but was downgraded for Saturday's contest officially to "Out." While Tony Rojas and Kooper Ebel anchor that linebacker room, Tatsch's absence is more notable in comparison to someone like Smith who was also downgraded in last week's injury report vs. Northwestern. That room still has Cael Brezina, but it will be Rojas and Ebel picking up a majority of the workload without Tatsch or Smith. Nnodim and Tatsch were the "Questionable" players earlier in the week, and now it's just Nnodim. The defensive tackle has played in three games for Penn State since Week 3 vs. Buffalo. He's logged eight total tackles and one tackle for loss. If Nnodim isn't good to go or is limited on Saturday in terms of snaps, defensive coordinator D'Anton Lynn might put a little more on Keanu Williams and Siale Taupaki. The two lead the Nittany Lions' tackle room in total tackles so far this season and have the most NCAA experience. Ty Blanding, Alijah Carnell, and Dallas Vakalahi haven't been impact players for Lynn, so it'll be interesting to see which one will pick up the pace against the Trojans to help out Williams and Taupaki. Notable USC injuries: Jahkeem Stewart, Trent Mosley, Mark Bowman, and Jide Abasiri listed as QUESTIONABLE The junior starter on defense has had 16 tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss, and one sack on the season (six games). If Abasiri is limited or downgraded to out before the game, Stewart's likelihood to step in and be an impact on the defense when also listed as questionable is doubtful. Another notable injury is starting left guard Hayden Treter listed as doubtful for Saturday night. He played in the first five games for USC as well as Kaylon Miller. Miller stepped in Week 5 vs. Washington as Treter was questionable and ultimately did not play. home.blurb: Andrew Babalola was the first offensive lineman to suffer an injury . Then Evan Link went out. And then starting right tackle Andrew Sprague suffered an undisclosed injury ahead of the UTEP game, and hasn't been back since. The Wolverines moved Link to left tackle and Blake Frazier to right tackle. Michigan was hopeful to use the bye week to get players healthy for its remaining seven games, but the outlook doesn't sound great for Sprague. While Sprague's timeline might be weeks out, it does sound like the Wolverines will get Babalola back very soon. "Andrew [Sprague], I'm not sure. It's way out there if he comes back. It's way out there," Whittingham said of Sprague's timeline. "To answer your question: He'll start practicing today. We'll gradually ramp him up throughout the week and see if he's ready to contribute this Saturday. He'll really help us if he can because we're really thin there and got some other guys dinged up in the Minnesota game that will be questionable. That will come out on Wednesday in the injury report." Michigan's starting guard Nate Efobi has also been dinged up, and it's possible he is one of the linemen Whittingham was referring to that will be questionable for the availability report. Michigan could use Babalola, a former five-star, back as soon as possible. While he has yet to play a college football game, we know the talent is there, and if the Wolverines feel that he will help them win — expect him to play. "It doesn't change the fact that he's not available or won't be available for several weeks. But at least we feel now that maybe they've got a handle on it — not a handle on it, but they've got some agreement on it. We sure miss him. He's a good player. He's a really good football player." Michigan's initial availability report for the game against Penn State will come out on Wednesday. It will be interesting to see who is on the list, and if the Wolverines are in danger of missing more starting linemen for the home game against the Nittany Lions . "Andrew Babalola, fortunately, will be able to start practice this week, which will be the first time in, what, a month. It's been a big disappointment for us because we were really counting on him.
